author: Antimilitarist*innen
title: Wedding: Glasbruch und Farbe bei Kriegsprofiteur Würth
content:
Als Antwort darauf, dass Sie eine Munitionsfabrik mitten in die Stadt setzen und diese mit der Schusswaffe verteidigen und in Solidarität mit allen, die Widerstand leisten und die Kriegsindustrie angreifen.

Am frühen morgen des 6. August haben wir in Berlin Wedding das Geschäft eines der Unternehmen besucht, das in die Rüstungsproduktion involviert ist und vom Krieg massiv profitiert. Wir haben einige Scheiben eingehämmert und Farbe verteilt. Damit rufen wir dazu auf, dezentral, unberechenbar und überall dagegen vorzugehen, dass unsere Kieze militarisiert werden und alles anzugreifen, was daran beteiligt ist.

Getroffen hat es dieses mal Würth in der Schulzendorfer Straße. Würth bezeichnet sich als der weltweit führende Konzern bei Befestigungs- und Montagetechnik, doch die recht unscheinbar wirkende Firma stellt auch Elektronikteile, Leiterplatten, Schalter und Schmierstoffe her. Geführt wird sie von Reinhold Würth, dem reichsten Deutschen mit einem Privatvermögen von 40 Milliarden Dollar.

Eine Strategie der Verantwortlichen von Würth ist es, nicht offen darüber zu reden, wofür genau ihre Produkte verwendet werden. Dies ist auch meist relativ effektiv, zumal es sich hauptsächlich um Massen- und Kleinstware handelt, wodurch es deutlich schwerer ist nachzuverfolgen wo all diese Teile eingesetzt werden. Doch muss davon ausgegangen werden, dass Teile von Würth vom U-Boot bis zum Satelliten in einem großen Teil westlicher militärischer Güter verbaut sind.

Schützenpanzer für Saudi-Arabien

Belastbare Informationen darüber sind jedoch rar und kommen nur zufällig ans Licht. 2019 zum Beispiel, als die deutsche Regierung nach der Ermordung des Journalisten Khashoggi ein Exportverbot für Rüstungslieferungen nach Saudi-Arabien verhängte. Da Würth Schalter für französische Schützenpanzer baute, die zu dieser Zeit der saudischen Polizei für ihre Gewaltexzesse übergeben werden sollten, stellte das Verbot für Würth ein Problem dar. Würth legte beim Bundesamt für Wirtschaft und Ausfuhrkontrolle Widerspruch gegen die Aussetzung einer Ausfuhrgenehmigung ein und hatte wohl mit Klage gedroht. Als dies an die Öffentlichkeit kam, beteuerte man scheinheilig, dass es nicht um „die Wiederinkraftsetzung der erteilten Ausfuhrgenehmigung, sondern ausschließlich die Schadloshaltung für einen eventuellen wirtschaftlichen Schaden“ ging. Sprich, dass, wenn schon Exportverbot, dann der Steuerzahler den Gewinnausfall ausgleichen sollte. Gemeinsam mit Rheinmetall, die natürlich auch von dem Exportverbot betroffen waren, handelte Würth in diesem Fall in Stellvertretung der deutschen Rüstungsindustrie, in dessen Lobbyverband, dem Bundesverband der Deutschen Sicherheits- und Verteidigungsindustrie, beide Firmen gemeinsam mit anderen Größen wie Thales, Siemens und Renk organisiert sind. (https://www.spiegel.de/wirtschaft/unternehmen/saudi-arabien-waffenliefer-verbot-wuerth-wehrt-sich-gegen-ruestungsexport-stopp-a-1253736.html) Würth ist damit genauso wie Rheinmetall als Profiteur und Treiber von Waffengeschäften und Krieg entlarvt. Genauer gesagt hat Würth mit der Belieferung von Saudi-Arabien erwiesenermaßen seit Jahren den Krieg in Westasien befeuert, sich auf der Seite eines Staates und damit gegen die Menschen, ihren Widerstand gegen Herrschaft und Besatzung und ihre Selbstorganisierung positioniert. Würth handelt damit in direkter Kontinuität des Kolonialismus und als Akteur des westlichen Imperialismus sowie als Helfer der heute u.a. vom saudischen Staat ausgehenden Bombardements im Iran.

Unter dem Label von Liqui Moly produziert Würth in Deutschland für den internationalen Markt ein weiteres unscheinbares aber essentiell kriegswichtiges Produkt: Schmierstoffe, d.h. Motoröle, Treibstoffzusätze und dergleichen. Dass kriegerische Zeiten gute Geschäfte bedeuten, sieht man am Anstieg der Erlöse der Marke Liqui Moly, so z.B. von 2024 auf 2025 um acht Prozent auf 1,1 Milliarden Euro. In der Vergangenheit hat Liqui Moly schon die US-Airforce versorgt. Heute wissen wir, dass die Ukraine an deutschem Liqui Moly hängt. Erst am 6. August 2026 wurde in Kiev ein Lagerhaus von Würth bombardiert und brannte komplett ab. Es hatte wohl Schmierstoffe für das Militär lagerte. Es wird von „massiven Auswirkungen auf die Warenversorgung in der Ukraine“ berichtet. Zuvor war schon über die Verlegung des Lagerhauses wegen der Bedrohung durch russische Raketenangriffe diskutiert worden.

Mit der Unterfirma Würth Aerospace ist der Konzern auch im Bundesverband der Luft …

author: David Swanson
title: Between Disaster and Foreign Interference: Lessons in Peace and Solidarity in the Wake of the Earthquake in Venezuela
content:
By IPB Council Member and WBW Latin America Organizer Gabriel Aguirre, August 9, 2026

Imagine returning home after a holiday and realizing you’ve lost everything: family, friends, acquaintances, your home, everything you once thought would be forever. This was the reality many Venezuelans faced after the double earthquake that struck the country on June 24th. According to experts, these seismic events measured 7.1 and 7.3 on the Richter scale, occurring just 39 seconds apart.

It’s impossible to describe the catastrophic consequences of this natural event. The last major earthquake in Venezuela was in 1967. Almost 60 years later, a more intense earthquake with more dramatic consequences struck. The earthquake primarily impacted three central states located in the northern coastal region of the country: La Guaira, Caracas, and Miranda. Other states were also affected, but to a lesser extent.

At the time of writing this report, more than 6,000 people have died, many are missing, and nearly 6,000 have been rescued from the rubble. Undoubtedly, in the aftermath of the earthquake in Venezuela, we must acknowledge the solidarity of the world, which immediately sent rescuers and humanitarian aid to the country. This, along with the actions of rescue teams, firefighters, and the country’s security forces, allowed for the rescue and care of a significant number of people.

Words cannot adequately express the solidarity of the Venezuelan people. From the very first day after June 24th, millions of people mobilized to help the earthquake victims with selfless, altruistic, and decisive action. Supplies, medicine, food, clothing, and all kinds of aid were provided and continue to be distributed. We, as peace activists, are mobilizing in an organized manner to provide assistance to those who need it most.

Among the countries that mobilized aid was the United States, with the peculiarity that its initial reaction was to send military troops and Southern Command personnel to the country, under the pretext of providing humanitarian assistance in response to the earthquake’s aftermath. This is undoubtedly an important point to analyze the implications of, especially since similar pretexts have been used in the past to justify military occupations, as happened in Haiti in 2010. Those of us who raise the banners of peace must always warn about the risks faced by the peoples of Latin America, because the plans for interference, subjugation, and colonialism remain intact.

The United States announced $300 billion in aid to address the emergency in Venezuela; however, it is currently withholding nearly $20 billion. Furthermore, it is responsible for the shortages faced by Venezuelan rescue teams due to over 12 years of sanctions against the country, the inability to import high-tech equipment, and the lack of funds to provide essential supplies to firefighters and other disaster relief groups.

Without a doubt, the IPB and pacifist organizations raise their voices for peace and demand the lifting of all sanctions against the country. It is time to allow the Venezuelan people the capacity and funds necessary to address this grave emergency.

The post Between Disaster and Foreign Interference: Lessons in Peace and Solidarity in the Wake of the Earthquake in Venezuela appeared first on World BEYOND War.

title: I coccodrilli di Ben Gvir sono l’ultima arma utilizzata da Israele nella sua guerra animale contro i palestinesi
content:
Dagli scritti coloniali di Herzl ai cani da attacco, dai cinghiali alle prigioni con fossato di coccodrilli, gli animali sono stati a lungo impiegati nel progetto sionista per terrorizzare i palestinesi.

Joseph Massad – 30 luglio 2026

Il 18 gennaio 2021, decine di coccodrilli furono trovati spiaggiati in una fattoria abbandonata vicino all’insediamento israeliano illegale di Petzael, nella valle del Giordano occupata.

All’inizio di questo mese, il ministro della Sicurezza nazionale israeliano Itamar Ben Gvir ha annunciato che Israele avrebbe utilizzato i coccodrilli del Nilo come guardie carcerarie per i prigionieri politici palestinesi .

Il programma inizierà presso il carcere di Ketziot, il più grande di Israele, nel deserto del Naqab (Negev). Il carcere è stato un campo di concentramento dove migliaia di palestinesi furono incarcerati tra il 1988 e il 1995 durante la Prima Intifada. I palestinesi conoscevano Ketziot come il campo di Ansar III.

Per agevolare questo piano, il Ministro della Protezione Ambientale Idit Silman ha dichiarato il coccodrillo “animale selvatico addomesticato”. In base a questa nuova classificazione, i rettili verranno liberati nei fossati che circondano le prigioni israeliane, dove i palestinesi sono imprigionati e trattati come animali.

Ben Gvir si è ispirato al nuovo centro di detenzione per migranti in Florida, soprannominato “Alcatraz degli alligatori”, visitato lo scorso anno dal presidente degli Stati Uniti Donald Trump . Questa prigione degli orrori “sorge in una vasta zona umida subtropicale infestata da alligatori, coccodrilli e pitoni”.

Si tratta di un caso in cui una colonia di insediamento ne ha ispirata un’altra.

Gli animali sono da tempo un elemento ricorrente nelle strategie israeliane per dominare e opprimere i palestinesi e per “riportare” la Palestina al suo passato ebraico idealizzato. I leader sionisti e israeliani hanno spesso paragonato i palestinesi agli animali, ma la guerra condotta da Israele contro gli animali va oltre le metafore e coinvolge animali reali.

I leader sionisti e israeliani hanno a lungo descritto i palestinesi come “animali”, spesso specificandone la specie.

Per giustificare l’avvio del genocidio a Gaza, ad esempio, l’allora ministro della Difesa israeliano Yoav Gallant definì i palestinesi “animali umani”.

Al contrario, negli anni ’60 e all’inizio degli anni ’70, il ministro della Difesa israeliano Moshe Dayan non poté scegliere a quale specie di insetti o mammiferi i palestinesi assomigliassero di più, e li chiamò “vespe” e “cani” nell’interesse della non discriminazione.

Per decenni, Israele ha usato gli animali per opprimere e umiliare i palestinesi, prendendo di mira entrambi con la sua macchina di morte

Negli anni ’80, il Primo Ministro israeliano Menachem Begin li elevò al rango di “bestie a due zampe”, mentre l’ex capo di stato maggiore israeliano Rafael Eitan li declassò nuovamente a ” scarafaggi “. Il Primo Ministro israeliano Yitzhak Shamir preferì la categoria entomologica, descrivendo i manifestanti palestinesi come ” cavallette “.

Ironicamente, nel 2000 il Primo Ministro Ehud Barak definì i palestinesi “coccodrilli”. Il piano di Ben Gvir, a quanto pare, è quello di far sì che dei veri coccodrilli proteggano quelli metaforici.

Al di là di similitudini e metafore, il piano del ministro non inaugura una guerra contro gli animali perpetrata contro i palestinesi. Per decenni, Israele ha utilizzato gli animali per opprimerli e umiliarli, prendendo di mira sia i palestinesi che i loro animali con la sua macchina di morte, trattandoli come appartenenti alla stessa specie.

In un agghiacciante reportage di Al Jazeera English del 28 novembre 2023, lo scrittore e poeta palestinese Refaat Alareer, volontario presso il comune di Gaza, accompagnava gli spettatori attraverso lo zoo cittadino devastato, documentando gli animali morti e affamati. Una settimana dopo, Israele avrebbe compiuto il famigerato assassinio di Alareer e di diversi membri della sua famiglia, nel contesto del genocidio in corso.

Oltre a uccidere gli animali palestinesi, i coloni israeliani li hanno anche rubati, insieme a bovini e altro bestiame palestinese. Israele ha persino rubato la vipera palestinese autoctona nel 2018 e l’ha dichiarata il suo “serpente nazionale”.

La preoccupazione sionista per gli animali, in particolare per i serpenti, risale al fondatore dell’Organizzazione Sionista, Theodor Herzl, che nei suoi diari delineò cosa si sarebbe dovuto fare …

author: Martina Jebet
title: Renegotiating Military Immunity: Kenya’s New Terms for Foreign Troops
content:
In July 2026, Britain suspended one of its flagship military exercises in Kenya after Nairobi withheld the licences required for troops to train in Laikipia. Five days later, the two governments reached an agreement allowing Exercise Haraka Storm to proceed. The immediate diplomatic crisis ended, but the deeper dispute did not; the standoff revealed that Kenya is no longer questioning the terms of Britain’s military presence but using licensing, parliamentary oversight, and domestic law to press for new legal terms governing how that presence operates.

The strategy has been in development for several years, and it owes much to the unresolved murder of Agnes Wanjiru. When a Kenyan court issued an arrest warrant for a former British soldier in September 2025, and he was subsequently arrested in the UK that November as he contested extradition, it crystallised a constitutional principle: that Kenyan courts have jurisdiction over crimes committed on Kenyan soil, regardless of the suspect’s nationality.

That assertion now sits at the centre of live negotiations for the renewal of the Defence Cooperation Agreement governing the British Army Training Unit in Kenya (BATUK), which remains under active parliamentary negotiation and is not yet finalised. In 2021, Kenya’s Parliament made a previous attempt to strip BATUK personnel of diplomatic immunity, which the UK rejected. The renewed negotiations now take place against a backdrop of years of litigation, parliamentary scrutiny, and renewed public scrutiny, and, as July demonstrated, a Kenyan government prepared to act on that pressure.

BATUK and the Accumulation of Grievances

The Wanjiru case is the most visible, but it is not the only one. Over decades, BATUK’s presence in Laikipia and Nanyuki has generated a series of disputes that have exposed gaps in the oversight mechanisms surrounding the agreement.

In August 2025, the UK government finalised an out-of-court settlement of £2.9 million for more than 7,700 claimants affected by the 2021 Lolldaiga Hills wildfire, which was linked to British military training exercises. Individual payouts ranged from around KES 22,500 to KES 2.5 million depending on the claim—sums many residents said bore little relation to years of lost livestock, health complications, and land damage. The UK did not admit liability. “The settlement was never just about compensation,” Charles Lawi, a community leader in Laikipia, told me. “It was about getting someone to admit responsibility.” For many advocates, the settlement’s existence proved that accountability was achievable, but its terms illustrated why ad hoc arrangements are an inadequate substitute for institutionalised legal responsibility.

Other grievances remain unresolved. Communities near training areas have documented long-running complaints about unexploded ordnance in farmland; parliament has repeatedly raised concerns about environmental damage from vehicle movements, live-fire exercises, and inadequate land rehabilitation; and Kenyan women have also sought legal recognition and child support for children allegedly fathered by British soldiers, exposing how little formal infrastructure exists to handle such claims.

Taken individually, each dispute can be managed, delayed, or minimised. Taken together, they describe a partnership that has operated with limited legal exposure—and a Kenyan public that is increasingly unwilling to accept that arrangement.

What the Negotiations Are Actually About

Neither Nairobi nor London has signalled an intention to terminate the defence partnership. Instead, the 2026 review has become an opportunity for Parliament, lawmakers, and affected communities to demand stronger legal safeguards. Civil society campaigns no longer confine the pressure. It is now evident in a parliamentary report that recommends fundamental changes to the legal framework governing BATUK.

In late 2025, the National Assembly’s Committee on Defence, Intelligence, and Foreign Relations published the findings of a two-year inquiry. The report documented allegations of sexual abuse, environmental harm, and negligence involving unexploded ordnance. It also criticised BATUK officers for declining to appear before the committee by citing diplomatic immunity, recommending that immunity be removed for serious crimes and that mechanisms be created to establish paternity and enforce child maintenance. The British High Commission later said its submission to the inquiry had not been …

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: BBC Axed Report on British Army Killing Unarmed Child in Derry
content:
The UK government successfully lobbied the BBC to axe a report revealing the British Army killed an unarmed child in Derry during the Troubles in 1972, newly released documents reveal. A week after 15-year-old Daniel Hegarty was shot dead, the Ministry of Defence falsely claimed he had been killed from a distance of 25 metres by a soldier who believed the child was armed. But a memo sent days after the 31 July incident showed senior personnel knew Hegarty had in fact been killed by a “general purpose machine gun” at point-blank range. Hegarty’s killer was an 18-year-old known only as ‘Soldier B’, who shot him during Operation Motorman, a British Army push to retake “no-go areas” controlled by residents and Irish republican paramilitaries. Soldier B reportedly told an October 1973 inquest: “I cocked the weapon and when the youths were about 25 metres away I aimed at the leading man and fired a quick burst” of bullets. The declassified documents, obtained by the Pat Finucane Centre, show that BBC Panorama correspondent Alan Hart spoke to witnesses of the shooting who said Hegarty and two cousins who were with him were unarmed and posed no threat.

Hart then approached the British Army in Derry for comment. His request reached the office of prime minister Edward Heath, whose press secretary Donald Maitland instructed a senior official at the Northern Ireland Office (NIO) to “persuade Panorama not to include this tragic incident in the projected programme”. The pressure worked, and the BBC omitted the segment when the programme aired on 7 August 1972. “After a major effort, the NIO managed to get the item removed from Monday’s programme,” NIO spokesperson RJ Seaman told the Ministry of Defence the following day.

Hegarty’s sister, Margaret Brady, told the Irish News last week: “We could have been spared decades of hurt and heartbreak if they had admitted what they knew, that Daniel was innocent, unarmed and shot at close range.”

Brady has called on the BBC to locate unaired footage of interviews with her parents in the aftermath of the killing. The corporation told Derry Journal it would “make every effort to locate the footage… although at this point we cannot say if it still exists.”

author: By Phil Mandelbaum, Contributor
title: Reporting from Gaza with Palestinian Poet Ahmed Sarsour
content:
“It’s not just about what’s happening in Palestine, it’s happening everywhere. The same forces that are controlling the world, the capitalist and imperialist forces, they are the ones who started the war in Sudan, and they are the ones waging wars in communities in every country in the world, like in Congo and Turtle Island, and Cuba and Venezuela,” Ahmed Sarsour tells me.

It’s the afternoon of Friday, June 26, and Sarsour is struggling to stay on the call amid interruptions in electricity. The 33-year-old Palestinian poet is speaking to Unicorn Riot from his birthplace, his grandparents’ home in the center of Gaza in the city of Deir Al-Balah. Shaken but still standing after three separate bombings, the house sits adjacent to rubble from their neighbors’ former home. The local mosque has also been destroyed.

“The Internet is not stable, there’s just a local vendor here in the Gaza Strip — and we are dependent on it because there hasn’t been electricity in Gaza since the seventh of October,” Sarsour says.

On October 7, 2023, Israel declared war, launching an attack on Gaza that has left the majority of Gaza’s 2.3 million people displaced. According to the official numbers reported nearly 75,000 Palestinians have been killed while researchers find the total could be fifty percent higher with a death toll surpassing 100,000 .

Unicorn Riot coverage from the frontlines in Gaza and Palestine

During our conversation, Sarsour mentions October 7 repeatedly, always to assert that “the genocide” didn’t begin that day.

Sarsour was born in Palestine to a gynecologist father and pharmacist mother. When he was nine, he and his four siblings followed their parents to Sudan. It was only supposed to be for a few years, while his father finished his studies, but the family decided to stay because for them Sudan represented “the best shot to have a better life, a good life.” As Sarsour explains, “Gaza has always been this rough.”

During this time, all the Sarsour children earned their degrees; the two brothers became engineers, and their sisters doctors.

Unfortunately, though, after two decades the family was forced to return to Palestine, “fleeing the war” in Sudan that started April 2023. “We tried to hold our ground and stay there because we built a life for almost 20 years there. We had everything there, and we left everything behind,” Sarsour tells me. “And we actually fled a war to get trapped in another genocide.”

Related: ‘Zaghrouda’ in the Midst of the Sudan War

When Sarsour first returned to Palestine, he focused on his family’s survival. Friends from Sudan contacted him in February 2024, asking why he hadn’t left. But he’d only recently returned, and the family couldn’t afford to leave. So, his friends started a GoFundMe page for the Sarsours — and, at least initially, the poet Sarsour was hopeful.

Social media users were calling Palestinians with fundraisers spammers and “profiteers who are trying to scam people.” So, Sarsour decided, “I need to put a face to the campaign.”

This is when, overcoming social anxiety, Sarsour took to social media in hopes of connecting with activists and influencers online, at which point he says he “started seeing the news.” And this is when he decided poetry was the way he’d respond.

“I had been seeing what’s happening in the north, what’s happening in the south, and it broke my heart, seeing all of these people getting murdered, and getting amputated, and no one cares about them… And they were recording themselves to the outside world to see, and yet people were calling them liars.”

“They always claim that these are Hamas members or terrorists, but even after the claimed ceasefire, these targets have been intensified,” he says. “And they are trying to target people during the most uncommon times, when they don’t expect it… During weddings, or festivities, or in the markets.”

Another example, Sarsour adds, is the targeting of fishermen — because “they don’t want Gazans to have any reliable source of food.”

Before returning to Palestine, Sarsour had written poems about the wars there “in 2012, 2014, 2018 and 2020, and all the other wars they waged in Gaza.” He’d written in his native language, Arabic, from his home in Sudan. And then for five years he didn’t write at all, feeling “really betrayed because no one cares, no one is listening.”

author: webadmin
title: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs uncover horrific scenes at industrial-scale gamebird rearing site
content:
Dead gamebirds burned in bonfire pits in breach of animal by-product regulations

Guest post by Wiltshire Hunt Sabs: In July, after being alerted alerted to illegal practises at a local shoot, they paid a visit to the Stockton Shoot in Wiltshire and what they found was truly horrific – a bonfire full of dead charred birds, set next to the industrial sized operation.

Bordering the shoot is Stockton Wood and Down a 61.5 hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), situated within approximately 500metres of the rearing pens. The site supports a diverse range of flora, including several rare and notable plant species, while its birdlife includes buzzards, green and great spotted woodpeckers, nuthatches, nightingales, lesser whitethroats and grasshopper warblers.

The environmental impacts of intensive pheasant releases are well documented. High densities of released gamebirds can alter woodland ecosystems, damage sensitive ground flora, enrich soils with excessive nutrients and cause long-term degradation around release pens. Guidance recommends rotating pen locations to allow habitats to recover and to provide fresh ground for successive flocks.

This site has to be seen to be believed. The scale is enormous, with many thousands of pheasants and partridges held within the rearing pens. Historic Google Earth imagery indicates that these pens have been used for many years and have expanded significantly over time, with little evidence that the release areas have been moved to allow environmental recovery.

As with any intensive bird-rearing operation, mortality rates are unavoidable. High stocking densities, parasites, disease, stress, feather pecking and predation all contribute to a continual accumulation of dead birds requiring lawful disposal.

Until they are released, these birds are legally classified as livestock, meaning their disposal is governed by strict animal by-product legislation designed to protect public health and prevent the spread of disease.

The law is clear. Fallen birds that have died other than by slaughter are classified as Category 2 animal by-products. They must be collected without undue delay, stored securely in sealed, leak-proof containers, and kept away from other animals before collection. Disposal must take place through licensed routes, such as approved rendering plants, incinerators, maggot farms or collection schemes operated through the National Fallen Stock Company.

The Direct Burial Or Burning On Farms is forbidden.

All video and imagery has been passed to the local authority ANIMAL HEALTH team within Public Health for investigation and the premises are under investigation.

Beyond the legal implications regarding public health, the disregard for basic fire safety was astonishing. Bonfires were observed on dry, sun-scorched grassland, surrounded by equally dry vegetation and in close proximity to numerous gas cylinders, during one of England’s hottest and driest summers. Such conditions present an obvious and serious fire risk, with potentially severe consequences for people, wildlife and the surrounding countryside.

This isn’t even the first time we have had to have this area investigated. Back in 2023 we found the neighbouring Fonthill Estate putting anti-coagulant rat poisons in the open countryside. This prompted a compliance visit from Natural England at the time. Dozens of poison containers dotted around in amongst the flora and fauna of the open countryside. It was reported a few days ago that rat poison was found in at least five dead sea eagles in nearby Dorset.

This is not an obscure, poorly managed shoot operating in some backwater. Given its prestige, resources and influence, the standards expected should be among the very highest in the country. Which begs the question, if this is one of the best, what must the backwaters shoots be like?

What we have documented raises serious questions about so-called environmental stewardship, biosecurity, animal welfare and regulatory compliance.

As with hunting, shoots see themselves above the law, and beyond its reach. We hope Wiltshire Council’s Animal Health team carries out a thorough investigation and that enforcement action should be taken without fear or favour, regardless of the shoot’s status or influence.

Please support the work of Wiltshire Hunt sabs here

The post Wiltshire Hunt Sabs uncover horrific scenes at industrial-scale gamebird rearing site appeared first on Hunt Saboteurs Association.

author: CNT Guadalajara
title: Bomberos Forestales veganos de Geacam queremos denunciar deficiencias en el avituallamiento del incendio de La Mierla
content:
Vaya por delante nuestro reconocimiento a la buena labor en general de la sección de logística desplegada para este incendio sabiendo lo complicado que puede llegar a ser con tal cantidad de efectivos, pero no podemos pasar por alto las deficiencias constatadas, con la intención de que estas sean subsanadas.

El avituallamiento en general ha sido bastante completo, café, leche, cacao y bollería en el Area de Espera, ensaladas de arroz, pasta, alubias y garbanzos, bocadillos variados (con alguna opción para vegetarianxs), flanes y puddings de chocolate y fruta.

Cada persona se llevaba un bocadillo a elegir, dos tuppers de ensalada a elegir, flan y pudding más dos piezas de fruta. Muy completo, variado y abundante.

Sin embargo, para lxs veganos ha sido un absoluto desastre, pareciera que al ser un colectivo poco representado en la empresa no se le presta la atención debida y obligada por ley.

Lxs veganxs, del avituallamiento detallado anteriormente, sólo podían coger tuppers de ensalada de alubias y garbanzos, además de piezas de fruta; y en el caso de lxs vegetarianos bocata de tortilla además de lo anterior. Del desayuno únicamente café sólo. Con el agravante de que las ensaladas referidas eran una lotería, al leer los ingredientes y alérgenos estaba claramente señalado que no contenían ningún tipo de producto animal, y sin embargo la gran mayoría de ellas contenían atún y pollo. Un error incomprensible y denunciable, es una vergüenza que una empresa de catering cometa un fallo de etiquetado tan burdo en los tiempos que corren.

Lejos de subsanarse tras señalarse desde los primeros días, incluso haciendo alguna sugerencia de opciones ofertadas años atrás, se ha convertido en norma, quedándose algún/x compañerx sin comer durante jornadas completas en un incendio en el que hemos trabajado a destajo durante más de diez días.

Todas merecemos el mismo trato, y recibir un avituallamiento suficiente y nutritivo es algo esencial en un trabajo duro y extenuante, no se puede obviar esa necesidad, máxime cuando se ha señalado desde los primeros días para que se solucionara.

Solicitamos a Geacam que rescinda el contrato con la empresa de catering, o se asegure de que va a proporcionar un avituallamiento en condiciones de igualdad con el del resto de componentes del dispositivo para lxs veganxs y vegetarianxs, como es obligatorio por ley.

La entrada Bomberos Forestales veganos de Geacam queremos denunciar deficiencias en el avituallamiento del incendio de La Mierla se publicó primero en Confederación Nacional del Trabajo.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als Mutterschwein in der Zucht zu leben
content:
Die Zucht von Schweinen ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet immer mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.

Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?

Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder – damit die Industrie deine Kinder töten und als „Schweinefleisch“ verkaufen kann.

Du bist gerade einmal etwas älter als ein halbes Jahr. Dann wirst du das erste Mal in einen Metallkäfig getrieben – den sogenannten Kastenstand. Er ist so eng, dass du dich nicht einmal umdrehen kannst. Du bist gefangen auf diesem einen Fleck. Du kannst nur stehen oder dich hinlegen. Das war’s.

Dann wirst du zwangsbefruchtet. Wenn die Befruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal klappt, wird der Vorgang wiederholt.

Fast vier Monate lang bist du schwanger.

Einen großen Teil deiner Schwangerschaft wirst du in einem Kastenstand fixiert. Alles ist trist, du hast keine Beschäftigung. Wochenlang kannst du dich kaum bewegen, geschweige denn andere natürliche Bedürfnisse ausleben.

Du bist eigentlich von Natur aus eine sehr fürsorgliche Mutter und kümmerst dich liebevoll um deine Kinder. Normalerweise würdest du für deine Ferkel ein Nest bauen. In der Fleischindustrie kannst du das alles aber nicht.

Du lebst auf kaltem, hartem Spaltenboden – Beton mit Schlitzen, durch die dein Kot und Urin fallen sollen. Deine Klauen sind verletzt und deine Gelenke schmerzen vom ständigen Stehen auf dieser rutschigen, harten Oberfläche.

Die Luft ist stickig. Durch die Güllekanäle unter dir steigt der beißende Ammoniakgeruch auf. Deine Atemwege werden davon verätzt, jeder deiner Atemzüge brennt.

Es ist laut, immer wieder schreien andere Schweine in der großen Halle. Reihe an Reihe fristet ihr euer Dasein.

Nachdem du die ersten Wochen deiner Schwangerschaft im Kastenstand verbringen musstest, kommst du einige Wochen vor deiner Geburt in den „Wartebereich mit Gruppenhaltung“. Auch dieser Bereich ist trist. Es gibt kaum Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten und unter dir ist wieder Spaltenboden. Du lebst dicht aneinander gedrängt mit anderen schwangeren Schweinen.

Kurz vor der Geburt deiner Kinder wirst du dann in eine sogenannte Abferkelbucht getrieben. Für dich bedeutet das wieder mehrere Wochen im Kastenstand, ohne dich bewegen zu können. Um dich herum wieder zahlreiche andere Tiere, unter dir der harte Spaltenboden.

Du bringst dieses Mal vierzehn Ferkel zur Welt. Sie sind winzig und auf dich angewiesen. Sie suchen deine Wärme, deine Zitzen. Du willst dich um sie kümmern, ihnen Nähe und Fürsorge geben, aber du kannst es nicht. Du bist im Käfig gefangen.

Eines deiner Kinder stirbt nur wenige Stunden nach der Geburt. Es ist zu schwach und kommt nicht an deine Zitzen. Ihm fehlt Wärme und Nahrung, aber du kannst nichts tun. Die Metallstäbe verhindern, dass du dein Junges erreichst. Es stirbt alleine. Du musst dabei zusehen, nur wenige Zentimeter von ihm entfernt.

Du wurdest so gezüchtet, dass du möglichst viele Ferkel „produzierst“. Viel mehr, als du natürlicherweise bekommen würdest. Dadurch kommen viele Ferkel sehr klein und schwach zur Welt oder sie sind krank. Du kannst nicht genug Milch produzieren, um sie alle zu versorgen. Manche verhungern qualvoll.

Oder sie werden von den Arbeiter*innen „aussortiert“. Selbst wenn eine medizinische Behandlung möglich wäre – für die Betriebe ist es häufig günstiger, die betroffenen Ferkel zu töten, als sie zu versorgen.

Ein Mensch packt eines deiner Ferkel, du kannst nichts tun und musst hilflos dabei zuschauen. Er betäubt dein Kind und schlitzt ihm anschließend mit einem Messer die Kehle auf – es stirbt und wird in den „Müll“ geworfen.

Die Industrie nennt den Käfig, in dem du eingesperrt bist, „Ferkelschutzkorb“. Er soll die Ferkel davor schützen, von dir erdrückt zu werden. Doch die Realität ist, dass genau das immer wieder passiert. Denn du hast keine Möglichkeit, deinen Kindern auszuweichen.

Deine Kinder suchen in der kargen und kalten Umgebung der Abferkelbucht deine Nähe. Dabei läuft eines unter dir. Aber irgendwann hast du keine Kraft mehr, auf deinen schmerzenden Beinen zu stehen. Du musst dich hinlegen und erdrückst dabei versehentlich dein eigenes Kind. Du hast keine Wahl, du bist an diesem Fleck gefangen und kannst nicht einfach zur Seite gehen, wie du es natürlicherweise machen würdest.

Deinen Ferkeln werden von den Menschen noch viele schlimme Dinge angetan. Ihnen werden die Schwänze abgetrennt und …

author: Tobias Sennhauser
title: Rückblick auf die Sommersession 2026
content:
Mercosur-Freihandelsabkommen

Das Freihandelsabkommen zwischen den EFTA-Staaten und Mercosur ( 26.033 ) soll den Handel mit Brasilien, Argentinien, Paraguay und Uruguay öffnen. Der Nationalrat lehnt die Vorlage mit 96 zu 86 Stimmen bei 9 Enthaltungen knapp ab. Zuvor waren mehrere Begleitmassnahmen gescheitert: die Übernahme der EU-Entwaldungsverordnung (108 zu 83 Stimmen), ein Agrarkredit von 880 Millionen Franken über acht Jahre (94 zu 91 Stimmen) sowie Anträge zu einem Amazonienfonds und gegen Zwangsarbeit. Nun ist der Ständerat am Zug.

SP und Grüne stimmten gegen die Vorlage, dafür waren FDP und GLP. Den Ausschlag gaben einige Nein-Stimmen aus der SVP- und der Mitte-Fraktion. Der Schweizer Bauernverband warnte vor zusätzlichen Importen und Druck auf die einheimischen Märkte. Der Wirtschaftsdachverband economiesuisse spricht hingegen von einem «fatalen Zeichen für den Wirtschaftsstandort» und fordert eine Korrektur durch den Ständerat.

Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF): Dieses Abkommen hätte Importe von Fleisch aus Ländern mit tieferen Tierschutz- und Umweltstandards erleichtert. Dieses Fleisch käme aus Produktionssystemen, die mit Entwaldung und Massentierhaltung verbunden sind. Wir lehnen das Freihandelsabkommen mit den Mercosur-Staaten ab und appellieren an den Ständerat, der grossen Kammer zu folgen und die Vorlage zu versenken.

Stopfleber-Initiative

Die Volksinitiative «Ja zum Importverbot für Stopfleber» ( 24.089 ) will die Einfuhr von Stopfleber verbieten. Nachdem sich der Nationalrat in der Frühjahrssession als Erstrat für einen indirekten Gegenentwurf (25.404) aussprach, folgte ihm nun der Ständerat mit 24 zu 15 Stimmen bei 3 Enthaltungen. Der Gegenentwurf verzichtet auf ein Importverbot und setzt stattdessen auf die bereits eingeführte Deklarationspflicht: Ab 2027 müssen Produkte von gestopften Enten und Gänsen den Hinweis tragen, dass sie unter für Tiere schmerzhaften Bedingungen erzeugt wurden. Der Bund soll die Importe beobachten und dem Parlament alle fünf Jahre Bericht erstatten.

Die bürgerliche Mehrheit und der Bundesrat lehnen ein Importverbot ab und verweisen auf internationale Handelsverpflichtungen und die schwierige Kontrolle verarbeiteter Produkte.

Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF): Eine Deklarationspflicht ist ein Hohn angesichts des Leids der Tiere. Wir halten an der Initiative und damit auch am Importverbot fest.

Importverbot für tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelze

Der Bundesrat verlängert am 5. Juni 2026 die Übergangsbestimmungen des Pelz-Importverbots, das am 1. Juli 2025 in Kraft getreten ist. Neu dürfen tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelzerzeugnisse erst ab dem 1. Juli 2029 nicht mehr eingeführt und ab dem 1. Juli 2030 nicht mehr verkauft werden. Die Pelzbranche soll damit Zeit erhalten, ihre Produktionssysteme an ein geplantes Zertifizierungsprogramm für angeblich nicht-tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelze anzupassen.

Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF): Für uns ist unverständlich, wieso die Pelzindustrie mehr Zeit erhält. Die Produktion von Pelzen geschieht meist in tierquälerischer, in der Schweiz verbotenen Haltungsbedingungen. Für die sogenannten Pelztiere bedeutet jeder Tag, an dem wir warten, Leid und Tod.

Kultiviertes Fleisch

Eine Motion ( 23.3941 ) verlangt, die Zulassungs- und Bewilligungsverfahren für neuartige Lebensmittel, insbesondere kultiviertes Fleisch und Produkte aus Präzisionsfermentation, zu vereinfachen und zu beschleunigen. Der Nationalrat hatte den Vorstoss in der Sondersession vom Mai 2025 mit 94 zu 87 Stimmen bei 8 Enthaltungen angenommen. Der Ständerat lehnte ihn am 8. Juni 2026 auf Antrag seiner Kommission und des Bundesrates stillschweigend ab. Damit ist die Motion erledigt.

Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF): Kultiviertes Fleisch könnte dazu beitragen, die Tötung von Tieren mittelfristig stark zu reduzieren. Für uns ist es deshalb unverständlich, gewaltfreie Alternativen zu blockieren. Die Ablehnung dieser Motion zementiert den Status quo der Tiernutzung.

Tiertransporte

Ab dem 1. Juli 2026 dürfen Tiere neu auch nachts sowie an Sonn- und Feiertagen transportiert werden. Bisher waren nur Transporte von Schlachttieren und Sportpferden vom Nacht- und Sonntagsfahrverbot ausgenommen; alle anderen Lebendtiertransporte brauchten eine kostenpflichtige Sonderbewilligung mit 48 Stunden Vorlauf. Mit der Anpassung der Verkehrsregelnverordnung entfällt dieses Einzelgesuch. Der Schweizer Tierschutz STS begrüsst die Änderung als «Gewinn fürs Tierwohl», weil Fahrten in …

author: Citizen Ilya
title: Wawancara dengan Aktivis Muda Food Not Bombs di Rusia
content:
Oleh:

Citizen Ilya

. Teks aslinya berjudul “

An Interview with Young Russian Activists from Food Not Bombs

”. Diterj

emahkan ke dalam Bahasa Indonesia oleh Ameyuri Ringo.


Support Ameyuri Ringo by considering becoming his

Patron

.


Food Not Bombs adalah gerakan internasional independen yang melakukan aksi langsung dengan membagikan makanan vegan kepada siapa saja yang membutuhkan. Para aktivisnya percaya bahwa kegiatan ini merupakan bagian dari perjuangan melawan kemiskinan, militerisme, dan kekerasan. Seluruh kelompok Food Not Bombs yang ada di Rusia beroperasi secara terdesentralisasi, tetapi tetap berpegang pada gagasan yang sama. Di tengah situasi ketika pemerintah Rusia menghabiskan miliaran rubel untuk anggaran militer, setidaknya 20 juta orang masih hidup di bawah garis kemiskinan. Kehadiran para aktivis antifasis muda ini telah membawa perubahan bagi banyak orang. Kami menghubungi beberapa aktivis Food Not Bombs di Samara untuk berbincang mengenai gerakan mereka.


1. Bisa ceritakan bagaimana gerakan ini muncul di Samara dan nilai-nilai apa yang kalian perjuangkan?


Andrew:

Gerakan ini mulai muncul di Samara pada tahun 2000-an. Saat itu para aktivis harus menghadapi serangan kelompok neo-Nazi. Mereka turun ke jalan dengan tutup panci di satu tangan dan pisau di tangan lainnya, mempertahankan diri dari serangan para neo-Nazi.


Kini situasinya sudah berubah. Jalanan jauh lebih aman, berkat mereka yang dahulu berani melawan para pelaku kekerasan tersebut. Generasi antifasis pun telah berganti.


Kami mulai mengorganisir kegiatan ini untuk menunjukkan bahwa orang-orang bisa melakukan kebaikan tanpa bergantung pada negara. Banyak dari kami merupakan pendukung komunisme libertarian, sementara banyak yang lain sekadar karena tidak bisa tinggal diam melihat penderitaan sesama.


Sekitar awal 2016 kami mulai aktif sebagai relawan, terutama dengan membantu tempat penampungan hewan. Pada Agustus 2018 kami mulai mempelajari pengalaman aktivis di Moskow dan St. Petersburg yang membagikan makanan kepada mereka yang membutuhkan. Pada akhir Oktober kami mengadakan aksi pertama. Sejak saat itu kami terus berjalan dengan mengandalkan sumber daya dan kemampuan kami sendiri, sambil perlahan membangun kekuatan bersama.


Oleg:

Gerakan ini sebenarnya berawal pada dekade 1980-an dan sejak itu menyebar ke berbagai belahan dunia, termasuk Rusia. Samara bukan pengecualian. Sepuluh hingga lima belas tahun lalu, aksi serupa juga pernah diadakan di kota ini. Kami hanya berusaha menghidupkannya kembali.


Tujuan utama gerakan ini adalah menarik perhatian publik terhadap kebijakan destruktif banyak pemerintah di dunia, yang menghabiskan dana besar untuk militer sementara jumlah orang miskin dan tunawisma terus bertambah akibat perang yang dimulai atau didukung oleh para penguasa.


Pada suatu titik, banyak dari kami merasa perlu melakukan sesuatu yang nyata daripada sekadar mengeluh tentang buruknya keadaan. Karena kami semua pernah mendengar tentang Food Not Bombs, kami memutuskan untuk menjalankan kegiatan semacam ini. Kami yakin kami mampu melakukannya, dan ternyata benar.


Masalahnya, kami tidak punya pengalaman dan tidak ada tempat untuk belajar. Namun kami tetap memulai. Sejak musim gugur tahun lalu kami rutin turun ke jalan membagikan makanan. Awalnya kami banyak belajar dari kesalahan sendiri. Setelah setiap aksi, kami mengevaluasi apa yang perlu diperbaiki atau ditambahkan. Kini kami memiliki cukup pengalaman dan dengan senang hati membagikannya kepada siapa saja yang ingin memulai kegiatan serupa.


2. Orang-orang seperti apa yang biasanya datang kepada kalian?


Andrew:

Sebagian besar yang kami bantu adalah para lansia yang harus bertahan hidup dengan uang pensiun yang sangat kecil. Selain itu ada juga pejalan kaki, pelajar, dan orang-orang yang tertarik dengan kegiatan kami lalu ikut makan bersama.


Oleg:

Beragam orang datang kepada kami. Ada tunawisma, warga lanjut usia, pekerja metro, pengunjung pasar, hingga orang yang sekadar lewat. Lokasi kami berada di antara stasiun metro dan pasar, jadi banyak orang singgah.


Sebagian datang untuk makan, tetapi ada juga yang ingin mengobrol, mencari tahu siapa kami, berbagi gagasan, atau menceritakan masalah yang mereka hadapi.


Kebanyakan mendukung apa yang kami lakukan, bahkan menawarkan bantuan. Namun ada juga yang bersikap negatif. Mereka percaya bahwa “orang yang tenggelam harus menyelamatkan dirinya sendiri.”

content:
Save the Date! Anarchie & Tierbefreiung – Strategie und Vernetzung in Zeiten von Kriegen, Rechtsruck und Klimakollaps
Vom 20. bis 23. März organisieren GgdT Bayern, Kollektiv Tierbefreiung Stuttgart/tierbefreier*innen Stuttgart und WATU ein Wochenende mit Workshops, Vorträge, bewegungsübergreifenden Austausch:
- Freitag, 20.03.26 bis Sonntag, 22.03.26 in Nürnberg
- Weitere Infos, Programm & Anmeldung folgen.
- Termin schon mal blocken – und bei Bedarf frühzeitig günstige Zugtickets sichern.
Rechtsruck, Militarisierung, Klimakollaps, Kriege, Sozialabbau – Wie organisieren wir uns weiter, wenn alles gleichzeitig eskaliert? Wie lässt sich noch Hoffnung und Kraft schöpfen?
Dieses Wochenende schafft Raum für Vernetzung, Strategie und gemeinsame Orientierung: für Menschen aus der Tierbefreiungsbewegung sowie aus anarchistischen, antifaschistischen, queer-feministischen und klimagerechten Kontexten.
Im Fokus stehen:
- Tierbefreiung als Teil eines intersektionalen, antikapitalistischen Befreiungskampfes
- Lernen voneinander: Tierbefreiung, Klimagerechtigkeitsbewegung, queer-feministische, autonome & anarchistische Praxis
- Umgang mit Erschöpfung und Verzweiflung – und Wege zurück zu Handlungsfähigkeit und Hoffnung
- Strategische Fragen: Was braucht die Bewegung? Was brauchen wir? Wie geht es weiter?
Geplant sind inhaltliche Workshops, Vorträge, bewegungsübergreifender Austausch, praktische Aktivismus-Skills, Räume für Selbstfürsorge – und viel Zeit für Vernetzung und gemeinsame Perspektiven.

GRENZENLOSER AUFRUF:


KOMMT MIT UNS IN DEN HAMBACHER FORST ZU EINER VERSAMMLUNG FÜR DIE TIERBEFREIUNG!


In den Massentierhaltungen und Vivisektionslaboren wehren sich unsere nichtmenschlichen Kameraden bereits. Die Zeit ist reif – lasst uns Fähigkeiten und Perspektiven austauschen, wie wir ihren Widerstand unterstützen können! Mit “Antispeziesismus” meinen wir nicht Online-Aktivismus, veganen Kapitalismus oder Bullen-umarmenden Pazifismus – wir eröffnen einen Raum, um gegen die menschliche Vorherrschaft vorzugehen, und wir brauchen keine bürokratischen Organisationen irgendeiner Art.


Viele Tierrechtsgruppen sind zu einer Brutstätte für faschistische/homophobe/cissexistische/macho/white supremacist/kolonialistische Ansichten und Verhaltensweisen geworden. Andere fördern den Liberalismus, den Staat oder stellen menschliche Aktivisten als “Tierretter” hin. Wir wollen auf zwei Jahren Anti-Spe Days aufbauen, die sich explizit gegen diese Tendenzen richten und kompromisslos alle Formen der Unterdrückung und Domestizierung ablehnen. Lasst uns einander treffen und Ärger machen!


Ihr könnt uns wieder im Hambacher Forst finden, einem der größten autonomen Räume Europas, der nach 10 Jahren immer noch besetzt ist. (Es ist ein Wald, also seid bereit zu campen).


Wir möchten, dass die Workshops dieses Jahr horizontaler sind – du kannst uns helfen, indem du deine eigenen vorschlägst! Einige Ideen, die wir bis jetzt haben:

Packt einen Schlafsack ein – und Kaffee und Erdnussbutter, wenn ihr welche habt! Kommt her, wie immer ihr könnt, und wir sehen uns im Juli!


Weitere Workshops und andere Informationen werden in der nächsten Zeit bekannt gegeben. Und meldet euch, wenn wir Fragen beantworten oder anderweitig helfen können.

author: Novara Media
title: Ex-Oil Engineer Turned Climate Whistleblower: We Face Collapse.
content:
The summer of 2026 will go down in history books as the hottest, driest and most deadly set of heatwaves Britain has ever experienced. This weather isn’t normal – but it is predictable according to a global consensus of scientists. And yet this summer, according to the science, will be one of the coolest summers we ever have again. Things will only get hotter from here.

Beginning his career as an oil-rig engineer before retraining as a climate scientist, Kevin Anderson’s career has been an extraordinary journey. On Downstream this week, Aaron Bastani sat down with him to discuss what has become his life’s work: sounding the alarm on man-made climate change, and on the fossil fuel industry that gave him his start.

Just how much has the planet heated, and why? Is the Paris Agreement’s aim of keeping heating to beneath 1.5°C still achievable, or delusional cope? What are the political obstacles to tackling the issue? Having worked with Andy Burnham in Manchester, what does Kevin think he will do on climate, as PM? Is avoiding catastrophe still possible, and if so, how much time have we got to act, before it’s too late?

author: Mekong Review 2
title: Letter from the mudflats Hai-Dang Phan
content:
Mud envelopes my feet, dark and cool, slick with sea. It’s low tide, and the sea has receded to reveal a massive mudflat stretching as far as the eye can see. We are at Tân Thành beach, roughly two hours by car from Saigon, on the coast of Vietnam’s Mekong Delta. It is early January—the dry season in the tropical south—when huge numbers of migratory shorebirds can be found on this expanse.

Following the lead of our guide, Ba and I cautiously navigate the ankle-deep water of a tidal channel. From atop the sea wall a storm-grey heron watches our slow progress. To the north and east, fishing huts perch high on bamboo posts. To the south, giant steel transmission towers dominate the horizon as they march offshore towards rows of wind turbines. On the muddy backshore, fishing boats lie stranded with nowhere to go, outsized eyes painted on their fading prows. They are the same kind of boats that my family used when we fled the country over forty years ago.

We are sloshing across the mudflats this morning because somewhere out there might be a spoon-billed sandpiper, one of the world’s rarest shorebirds and a critically endangered species. A few regular, if elusive, birds are recorded every winter here at Tân Thành. Our guide is Bùi Thành Trung—or, as he prefers it, Toby. He’s one the best birders in Vietnam, a shorebird specialist with a knack for finding “spoonies”, as he affectionately calls them.

“Stay inside the channel!” Toby shouts, spotting scope balanced over a shoulder. We have about two hours before the tide makes it too dangerous to be wandering the mudflats. We aren’t the only ones making the most of low tide. Further out, dozens of local women are digging for clams.

The watery path leads to the first set of makeshift bamboo “monkey bridges” we’ll need to cross. My seventy-four-year-old father stops in his tracks, considers the 30-metre obstacle course, his old knees, his bad balance, and tells us “kids” to go ahead without him. But Toby has just the pep talk. “You’re still cứng” he says, clenching his fist and smiling—still hard, still tough. That’s all it takes; Ba comes along.

There is something simultaneously exhilarating and comforting about being at Tân Thành. There’s no point bothering with footwear because they’ll only get stuck in the mud. Earlier, the act of taking off our shoes before setting foot on the mudflat called to mind the familiar Asian custom before entering a home. We are, after all, guests here in what Toby calls “Spoonyland”.

For the past few days, Ba and I have been on a meandering road trip through the Mekong Delta, from Saigon to the river town of Châu Đốc near Cambodia. He wanted to show me some of the places where he was stationed and fought during the war, some fifty years ago, as an officer of a patrol boat unit in the South Vietnamese Navy.

Today, we return to our primary mission: to experience Vietnam through its birds. Whenever we returned to Vietnam in the past, we usually spent all our time visiting family. For once, I wanted to see the country itself. On this matter, Ba and I found common ground. While he’s no avid birdwatcher like me, Ba likes a good challenge and wants to see as much of Vietnam as he still can.

Given the country’s long, distinctive coastline, a trip focused on shorebirds seemed essential, and searching for the spoon-billed sandpiper offered us a chance to do something extraordinary: witness a bird brought back from the brink of extinction. The guide I initially contacted was unavailable, but put me in touch with his friend, Toby. I knew about Toby from eBird, an online platform that birdwatchers the world over use to record and share sightings. Toby was the top “lister” in Vietnam, with 750 species observed—a distinction that filled me with unexpected pride when I first saw his Vietnamese name on top of a leaderboard stacked with Anglo-sounding names.

Toby studied business administration and held a decent desk job for an industrial sales company. Then, one day, a brief encounter with a sunbird ignited his passion for birds. More than ten years later, Toby has explored nearly every province in Vietnam on a quest to photograph every bird species in the country.

Reaching the sandbar peninsula, we catch our first glimpse of the shorebirds. I can’t make most of them out; they are only shapes flying back and forth. The birds are everywhere, in disorienting abundance, in wondrous array. How the hell are we going to find a tiny “spoonie”—a bird the …

title: "Fire Climate": Hot, Dry, Windy Days Are Becoming Common, Making Wildfires Harder to Control
content:
The Pacific Northwest is facing its worst fire season in more than 30 years. Scientists say drought, extreme heat and climate change are making wildfire seasons longer, more frequent and more destructive across the western United States.

“The homes, the communities, they’re just not simply prepared for fire,” says Paul Hessburg, former senior research ecologist at the U.S. Forest Service and professor of fire and landscape ecology at the University of Washington. Hessburg walks us through the history of the region, from the controlled fires practiced by Indigenous peoples before European settlement to present-day ecologically unsound factors including “accidental ignitions, dense forests, the wrong kinds of fuels on the ground [and] rapidly changing climate.”

author: Vivian La
title: A controversial plan to update Line 5 just suffered a major loss at the Michigan Supreme Court
content:
In a win for opponents of Enbridge Energy’s Line 5 pipeline, the Michigan Supreme Court vacated a key permit last week for a proposed project that would replace a segment of the pipeline running underneath an environmentally-sensitive area of the Great Lakes, finding that a state commission did not examine the full scope of possible harm to the environment.

Following the 6-1 decision, the justices remanded the permit back to the Michigan Public Service Commission for a more thorough review, which likely extends the timeline for a decision on a project that’s already been mired in legal and procedural hurdles for years.

Enbridge Energy received the permit in 2023 for its proposal to replace a segment of the oil and natural gas liquids pipeline — which connects lakes Michigan and Huron via the Straits of Mackinac — with a new one encased in a tunnel buried in the lakebed. Environmental groups and tribal nations appealed the decision, landing the case before the state’s highest court this year.

Writing for a nearly unanimous court in a 58-page opinion , Justice Elizabeth Welch said that the commission didn’t consider the full range of potential environmental harms, nor did it look at how the project would impact the public’s right to use the state’s natural resources, which includes the Great Lakes — protections granted under the state’s public trust doctrine.

“We cannot fault (the commission) for this failure, because there was little authority on this issue prior to our decision today. Even so, it was error,” the opinion stated.

Justices found that the commission incorrectly limited its scope of review under the Michigan Environmental Protection Act to just the tunnel, when it should have examined how the project would impact the broader pipeline. Line 5 transports crude oil and natural gas liquids 645 miles from Superior, Wisconsin, through Michigan to Sarnia, Ontario, with 4.5 miles of the pipeline crossing the straits.

In its new review, the justices said that the public service commission must answer whether the tunnel project will extend the lifespan of the 73-year-old pipeline, and if it does, determine what impacts there are to the environment and to the public trust.

“It is impossible to prevent or mitigate an environmental risk without understanding the nature of that risk,” the justices wrote.

Lawyers for the plaintiffs — four tribal nations across Michigan and three environmental groups — argued that because the tunnel project would extend the pipeline’s lifespan, it causes harm by increasing the risk of oil spills along Line 5’s entirety and increased greenhouse gas emissions from the fossil fuels it transports.

“The court has made clear that our understanding of environmental harm, it’s a practical understanding, but it’s also a broad one,” said Chad Hughes, senior attorney for the Environmental Law & Policy Center, which argued with the plaintiffs. “There’s no requirement to narrowly focus on the physical location of the project. You look at the environmental harms where they happen.”

By broadening the scope of reviews under the Michigan Environmental Protection Act, opponents said conversations about shutting down the entire pipeline are finally a possibility. The justices wrote that “a meaningful examination” of alternatives can’t happen until the commission determines the full impacts of the project.

“The door has been kicked open to an imaginable future where we can talk about alternatives other than Line 5,” said President Whitney Gravelle of the Bay Mills Indian Community, one of the plaintiffs in the case.

In a statement, Enbridge spokesperson Ryan Duffy wrote that the company disagrees and is disappointed by the ruling, calling it an additional delay to a project that has already been under review for nearly a decade. Enbridge is reviewing the opinion and assessing legal options, he said.

“What remains unchanged is our commitment to operating Line 5 safely and responsibly, incorporating enhanced safety measures in the Straits, and protecting Michigan’s natural resources for generations to come,” the statement said.

The lone dissenting opinion from Justice Brian Zahra said that the court’s directive to consider the full scope of potential harms was “a moral hazard,” because state regulators already decided Line 5 was in the public interest when it approved construction more than 70 years ago.

But Zahra agreed with the majority on the requirement to consider the public trust …

author: Adem Ay
title: How creativity — and children — have kept Albania’s revolution alive
content:
This article How creativity — and children — have kept Albania’s revolution alive was originally published by Waging Nonviolence .

It was on the third day of the revolution that the mood changed. Once again, many thousands of Albanians had descended on Tirana’s central square after work. Once again, the speeches and banners were focused on stopping a wild and legally protected coastline from being razed for a luxury resort. But this time the vibe was tense. Some people had entered the crowd who were angry, screaming abuses and trying to set fire to the placards.

Ilir Kaso, an artist and lecturer at Tirana University of Arts, stood nearby with his two daughters, aged 11 and seven. “My daughters were very frightened. My youngest asked to leave the protest, and so we did,” recalled Kaso. But as they emerged from the crowd, they found themselves facing what Kaso describes as “the flamingo group,” a collection of a hundred or so protesters wielding pink flamingo banners and a few pink polystyrene flamingos on poles. “‘Papa look, flamingos, let’s go there,’ said my youngest, and immediately I understood what we had to do.”

The flamingo group was a loose coalition of artists and environmental activists based in Tirana. The partnership had first formed more than a decade earlier under the banner of “Friends of Vjosa,” a movement to stop one of Europe’s last wild rivers from being splintered by 45 hydroelectric dams. Kaso became a part of what proved to be a very successful campaign. It birthed Europe’s first Wild River National Park, and on a personal level, it transformed Kaso’s art, pulling him away from abstraction and towards nature. He and his wife named their first daughter after the river.

When trucks and bulldozers suddenly rolled into a protected part of the river’s delta in late April, and started fencing off a large section of the coastline, the coalition quickly remobilized, meeting in person and via WhatsApp groups to work out how to stop the destruction. Kaso attended the first small protests along the fence line, photographing the flattening of ancient sand dunes where turtles nested, and the laying of concrete over wetlands that host hundreds of migratory bird species, many of them endangered.

Kaso had followed but not posted in the WhatsApp debate over which bird should be the symbol of their campaign. The environmental activists wanted one of the more threatened species to be made prominent — the Dalmatian pelican, the Northern lapwing — but the artists had decided on the flamingo, an easily recognizable bird with an iconic color and shape. After seeing how the bird had become a refuge for his frightened children, Kaso quickly started tapping out a message in the chat.

“I wrote about what happened and how we could create somewhere stationary, a shelter where we flamingos can stay all together and bring in the children, to protect them but also to expand the good vibes,” he said. “Because children have such good energy, they don’t have doubts or traumas like us. And we cannot wait for this protest to be damaged and become violent. This bad energy is going to destroy everything. We have to fight this with good energy, but by going out of the crowd.”

Kaso had experience setting up a shelter like this. During the pandemic he had helped to open and run a community school for his daughters and other young children in his area. The experience had a profound effect on how he taught his art students. After the pandemic, he rejected rigid lesson plans and formulas to be more curious and open to their ideas. “The children taught me a lot,” he said with a smile.

The artists and activists in the WhatsApp chat immediately embraced Kaso’s idea. Not only was there a shared fear of violence derailing this uprising, but the surging size of the crowds was clearly straining families. Every evening, between the speeches on the square, messages were going out over the microphone about lost children who needed to be found. On the chat, artists started offering to bring coloring pens and run drawing sessions. The next day, 20 feet of paper was laid out beside the Pyramid of Tirana, a tree-lined landmark between the square where protesters gathered and the prime minister’s office that they marched to. It was instantly flooded with grateful parents and curious children.

The Children’s Corner, as it is now called, has become an established feature of the revolution, entertaining children for approximately three hours every …

author: anarchy
title: The bane of Murray Bookchin Thought
content:
Murray Bookchin is rightly remembered for many things. He was a self-declared anarchist for a little more than three decades; according to the hagiography written by his long-term partner he became one in the late 1950s after moving away from the Stalinism of his youth, but he didn’t become known as one under his own name until the late 60s. Plenty of other anarchists found his analyses and positions to be lacking – he abandoned class struggle in the early 70s, tried to make common cause with the nascent right-wing “anarchists” of the Libertarian Party around the same time (even speaking at one of their conventions!), offered extremely uncritical support for the Sandinistas (because their red and black flag symbolised their adherence to anarcho-syndicalism – I’m not kidding), maintained a stubbornly inexplicable adherence to a Marxoid Hegelianism, and had a love-hate relationship with electoral politics by co-founding a local chapter of the Green Party.

By the mid-1980s, many of his critics had accused him of veering away from the recognisable principles of anarchism, an allegation he studiously ignored. His bitterness at being rejected as a leading figure of American – let alone international – anarchism, of an American Left Green caucus, or as anything more than a lecturer at a small private college where he directed the Institute for Social Ecology (ISE), led him eventually to slide into increasing irrelevance. He finally quit play acting, abandoning all pretence to being an anarchist – privately by 1995 and publicly in 1999.

Among his lingering legacies for anarchists are his ecological thought outlined in The Ecology of Freedom (1982), and his attacks on anarchists who didn’t toe his particular line. The former were long surpassed by works less enamoured with industrial technology, while the latter remained unsurpassed until the publication of the unintentionally hilarious Black Flame in 2009 (in which the authors outdid Bookchin, calling him out for even accepting that his targets were anarchists at all). According to his partner Janet Biehl, Bookchin told a few people that he was taking himself out of the club at the same time he wrote Social Anarchism or Lifestyle Anarchism: An Unbridgeable Chasm . This long essay is an incoherent screed, because there is no such thing as a “lifestyle anarchist”; in it, he denounced everyone he didn’t like who still wanted to be in the club, lumping their contradictory tendencies (neo-Situationists, hedonists, individualists, adventurists, postmodernists, apolitical anti-organisationalists, pluralists, Yuppies, and other avatars of “social reaction”) into a single scapegoat meant to explain the lack of popularity of some Official Anarchism.

And once he had sown more discord than any other single Anglophone anarchist, he walked away from the debate, leaving rancour and denunciation in his wake. In its stead, he created a vulgar Hegelian hybrid of allegedly vigorous Marxist analysis and weak left-wing social democratic practise, agrarianism and urbanism, bureaucratic centralisation and “libertarian municipalism” called communalism . This idiosyncratic invention, not anarchism, is what allegedly influenced the imprisoned Marxist Öcalan to push for an improved version of Kurdish nationalism, which, naturally enough, kept plenty of room for an official leadership and a historically hierarchical party structure. Apparently, every pro-PKK/YPG anarchist missed that memo.

There has never been a shortage of anarchists who get annoyed at other anarchists for ruining their club, but Bookchin’s caricature, the “lifestyle anarchist,” has bizarrely maintained a certain cachet among sectarians. This, despite the mismatched jumble of characteristics he cobbled together, and the documented revelation of his simultaneous rejection of anarchism – not just the “lifestyle” heresy. That he turned away from anarchism at the same time he slammed the tendencies that he found annoying should make even the most sectarian among us pause to consider the taint of Bookchin not actually wanting to “save” anarchism when his screed was published. Critical responses to SALA as well as other aspects of Murray Bookchin Thought include works by Bob Black , David Watson , Jason McQuinn , and others.

Meanwhile, two of the brightest stars in the ISE constellation, John Clark and Chuck Morse , came out of these destructive discussions with their eyes opened to much of what was wrong in Murray Bookchin Thought …

author: winter oak
title: The Erotic Life of a Mystic
content:
by Mark Josephs (aka Mark the Mystic Activist)

This is the most intimate article I’ve ever written. In it I describe my personal experience of awakening in an interconnected world in which everything is relating with everything.

Why do I define myself as a mystic? Because I look like one? Because I’m an old man living by myself, out in the countryside, off-grid, in a caravan? Because I wash outside, and meditate and pray? No.

I define myself as a mystic because my primary moment-to-moment interest is not in what’s happening, or even in what I’m doing – but in my relationship with The Totality (by whatever name).

When somebody prays, they feel they are in relationship with The Totality / God / Goddess / Great Mystery – obviously. But when somebody meditates deeply and “becomes one with everything”, there’s still the “with” word. That´s to say – there’s still a feeling of being in relationship.

I am interested in this relationship. I am interested in living in this relationship.

But first: the difficult question (and you might not like the answer!): is this relationship real? I might feel I am in relationship with The Totality, or my Idea of God or The Goddess – but does It feel Itself to be in relationship with me? Or (to be blunt): am I just imagining it?

I could give you clever answers about the infinite, interconnected complexity of existence, and the necessity of a coordinating intelligence – but any intellectual answer is only as reliable as the intellect. And the human intellect is clearly limited.

So let me be honest. I spend my days feeling I am in communion with The Totality. But am I really? I have no idea! Nor do I know how I could know!

I could make an appeal to the objectivity of intuition (“I just somehow know it to be true”), or to the objectivity of emotion (“I know it to be true because I can feel it”) – but, again, let’s be honest (otherwise what’s the point of discussing these matters: to just affirm each other’s preconceptions?): like the intellect, our intuitions and emotions are also subjective, conditioned and fallible.

But the exact same doubts about the reality of our perception apply to everything. How can we be certain of anything?! We perceive everything through limited, subjective, conditioned, fallible faculties! Does your lover love you? They say they do. You feel they do. But do they really? Can you prove it? No.

The truth of the matter, I believe, is that the only thing we can be certain of is uncertainty. Or, as Socrates reportedly declared: “I am the wisest of all, because I know I don’t know”.

We live in The Unknown. We don’t know where we are, or why. We don’t even perceive the world directly, but see its reflection on the screen of the mind – and therefore can’t even be certain of its reality. And so on.

So what to do? As Alan Watts said, “you´ve got to place your bet”. Your life is your betting chip, and you have to decide where to place it – whether on Universal Meaning or Universal Meaninglessness or Hedonism or Moralism or Guru Whoever or That Book… There are, of course, plenty of options.

So I have placed my bet, yes – on an ever-deepening relationship with The Totality. And as well as following Alan Watts’ advice, I also follow Joseph Campbell’s advice to “follow your bliss”. And he’s not talking about pleasure-seeking – he’s talking about something less easily defined: following that which makes our heart sing, following “the call of the soul” (John O’Donohue), following “the innermost decision that we cannot but obey” (Leonard Cohen).

I follow my bliss. And as I follow, the bliss increases! Does that prove the reality of Relationship with The Totality? (“You see – the relationship must be real, because the bliss just grows and grows!”) Not at all. It might just be that my hallucinatory state is expanding!

But what, for me, is this experience of relationship really like? I say it’s blissful. What else? What do I actually experience? What’s it like, for me, here in The Unknown, having placed my life-bet on the possibility of a real, reciprocatory relationship with The Totality?

The devotees of Krishna, the Sufis, and Christian mystics like Teresa of Avila and John of The Cross have all spoken of an erotic connection with The Totality. And I make this ‘appeal to authority’ (“you see, it’s not just me!”) because I am aware that people who speak about Sex with God (to be direct) can be easily misunderstood, and easily dismissed.

I don’t know exactly what …

author: agnes
title: The Price of Gold: The Xingu River and the Communities Facing Destruction
content:
The Price of Gold: The Xingu River and the Communities Facing Destruction


Country


Brazil


agnes


Tue, 07/28/2026 - 10:50


Issues


Human Rights


Program


5


Main Image


By Angel Ferreira

(Payayá, CS Intern)


At Volta Grande do Xingu, Brazil, two Indigenous communities, the Arara da Volta Grande and the Yudjá, continue to defend their ancestral territories against mounting external pressures. For the Yudjá, their name carries profound significance: it affirms their sovereignty and enduring relationship with the Xingu River, a bond that shapes their identity, culture, and way of life.


Today, however, their traditional livelihoods face a severe threat. The Volta Grande Project, backed by an estimated $229 million investment from Belo Sun Mineração Ltda., a subsidiary of Belo Sun Mining Corp., aims to establish one of the largest open-pit gold mines in the region. Community leaders and environmental experts warn that the project could inflict irreversible damage on a river system already deeply destabilized by the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Dam.


To understand the technical, social, and legal dimensions of this ongoing struggle, Cultural Survival spoke with anthropologist Thais Mantovanelli from the Instituto Socioambiental (ISA) / Xingu Program.


Thais Mantovanelli.


 


CS: With your experience of over a decade following the Juruna-Yudjá and Xikrin Peoples as well as the riverside communities, how are the mere expectations and pressure of Belo Sun's arrival already altering the social dynamics and mental health of these communities?


Thais Mantovanelli:

The Volta Grande do Xingu region, composed of three Indigenous territories and hundreds of riverine families where Belo Sun intends to establish itself, currently faces the risk of reaching a point of no return, both environmentally and in terms of the social conditions required for the physical and cultural reproduction of these Peoples. This is because the chain of impacts from the operation system of the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Power Plant has weakened the region's ecological and social system far more aggressively than anticipated in the project's environmental impact studies. This terrifying scenario is well known to these collectives, whose current and ancestral traditional knowledge reinforces this catastrophic assessment.


Given this backdrop, the prospect of a mining project aiming to become the largest open-pit gold mine in the country severely impacts their social dynamics and mental health. It is an attack on the future of coming generations and on the maintenance of a cultural system intrinsically linked to the flood pulse of the Xingu River and its tributaries.


A climate of dread now governs the daily lives of these families, who are forced to mentally cope with the risk of human contamination associated with the mining project. The venture could cause shocks and instability in Belo Monte’s structures, such as the Pimental dam and other dikes, as well as the risk of a tailings dam failure, similar to what occurred in Brumadinho and Mariana. Other threats include the scaring off and poisoning of land animals on the islands; impacts on birds due to noise pollution from explosives (projected to operate 24/7 for at least 12 years); the death of fish species already scarce due to Belo Monte’s operating system; navigation risks; airborne pollutant dispersion; pressure on the territory caused by an influx of workers; and risks of sexual violence against girls and women in the territory due to the increase in unknown men arriving to join the mining project's workforce.


The threat of Belo Sun's installation represents a massive strain on the mental health of these collectives, who lose control over the management of their lives in both the present and the future.


CS: Volta Grande do Xingu is already experiencing ecocide caused by Belo Monte's "consensus hydrogram." From an anthropological and subsistence perspective, what would the overlay of a mega gold-mining project mean for these Peoples in this context of water scarcity?
