title: Hilma Hofstedt - Agitationen - På uppviglarstråt i Gästrikland
content:
Författare

: Hilma Hofstedt

Titel

: Agitationen - På uppviglarstråt i Gästrikland

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #37 1916


 Jag var sömnig och ruskig när tåget stannade i Gävle, men jag blev strax klarvaken när jag fick se ett bekant ansikte vid spärren. Det var en Göteborgsgrabb, nu pamp för sjömans- och eldarunionen. Han förklarade helt bestämt att staden var den sovande staden. Vi tågade nu ut att bese den och vacker var den i alla fall. På kvällen voro vi i Bomhus och mötet var väl besökt och livligt applåderat. Där arbetar en L. S. under högtryck och det är inte småsaker de uträttat för att höja sin livsstandard. Men skulle ni inte också ha plats för klubben? Den har nog trots allt en plats att fylla. Söndagen gick färden till Forsbacka där Järn- och Metallarbetarf anordnat möte på eftermiddagen.


 Det blev gott besökt trots den olämpliga tiden; det är en fackförening som bär sitt namn med heder. De taga med glädje mot alla våra agitatorer och det vill inte säga litet det, att våga vara

så

 självständiga. På kvällen talade jag i Torsåker på rama bondbygden för fåtalig publik.


 Men vad jag beundrar dessa ihärdiga kamrater därute som i åratal förmått att hålla klubben vid liv mitt ute på »bondvichan.» Det är då ett manande exempel för oss att inte häller tröttna. Måndag var en fridag, då jag försökte mig på bärplockning, men resultatet blev 0.


 Tisdag var i Hofors, det var ett ganska bra möte med många bussiga anläggningsarbetare som åhörare. När man träffar

det

 folket blir man alltid vid gott humör. Onsdag Sandviken. Det blev ett storslaget möte med många hundra åhörare, men så höll jag också föredrag på en plats mitt inne i samhället. Där var folk från alla samhällsklasser. Det skadar inte. Tvärtom. Det gör dem gott att en gång få höra sanningen om ungsocialismen.


 Torsdag gick färden till Hammarby. En idyllisk plats inne i skogen. Mötet var besökt av ett hundratal personer, vilket man påstod var stor publik på den platsen, men nog skulle den kunnat vara större. Fredag besöktes Åshammar, men nu var det vädret som strejkade. Det regnade och enär mötet var anordnat utomhus blev det endast ett femtiotal åhörare. Lördag hade Kungsgårdskamraterna i samband med soc.-dem. klubben anordnat fest på sin vackra festplats och allt skulle utan tvivel varit trevligt om inte en hel del berusade individer hedrat platsen med sin närvaro. Dessa ha ju alltid förmåga att göra allting otrevligt. Det är beklagansvärt att inte arbetare efter så många års upplysningsarbete kan uppträda som människor vid sina fester. De skulle helt enkelt nekas tillträde, till dess de lärde vanligt folkvett. För övrigt var festen bra besökt och trevligt ordnad.


 Söndag återvände jag till den sovande staden, men den dagen bar den just ej skäl för namnet då det ena föredraget avlöste det andra hela eftermiddagen. I Boulogneskogen talade jag först inför en skara som ingen räkna kunge. Strax efter kom frälsningshären. Därefter en svensk frälsningshär och sist vår Gustav Sjöström, bokbindaren ni vet, och folk var på alla mötena. På kvällen talade jag i Elvkarleö inför så stor publik som lokalen kunde rymma. I Forsbacka fick vi en kommissionär för

Brand

, de övriga platserna ha vi klubbar. Men de måste bli större än nu. Därför fram för fortsatt agitation. Våra fiender rustar sig till strid. Må vi göra detsamma!


 Så var denna min lilla utomordentligt vällyckade tripp slut. Och nu ett tack och hälsning till alla klubbar och kamrater och på snarligt återseende. Med handslag.

author: Unknown
title: Fredrik Framstegsson - Revolt!
content:
Författare

: Fredrik Framstegsson

Titel

: Revolt!

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #7 1915


 Vill du bida alltjämt på den ljusare tid

 som har låvats dig, du proletär -

 vill du tro på en vila och stilla frid

 för de slavandes väldiga här

 utan kamp, utan strid, utan eniga män!

 Nej! slunga tillbaka den tron, min vän,

 på dem som den givit och slut dig stolt

 till den trasklädda hopens revolt!


 Du har fötts uti nöd, du har slavat i sot,

 du har pinats se'n ungdomens dar,

 du har skymfats, men tigit och tagit emot,

 fast du gömt i ditt innersta kvar

 en brand som förlamar, en brand som förtär -

 den elden skall flamma den gång, proletär,

 då du ställer dig högrest och stark och stolt

 i den trasklädda hopens revolt!


 Den elden, som tänts i din barm en gång,

 den kan inte slockna så lätt,

 den näres av årens sugande tvång,

 av skymf och av hån på allt sätt -

 den skall giva dig värme och kraft den tid,

 då äntligt du ställer dig fram till strid

 som en man, en beslutsam, en trotsigt stolt

 i den trasklädda hopens revolt!


 Se skaran, som tågar mot frihetens land

 - en här utav armodets barn -

 se bojor som splittrats, se lossade band,

 se, tömd står en grottekvarn!

 Och vet, att de tåga sin lycka emot,

 att våldet är krossat inför dess fot!

 Så, kasta ditt ok, proletär! Följ stolt

 med den trasklädda hopens revolt!

author: Unknown
title: Cómo forzamos que UPS creará empleos a tiempo completo en nuestra sección sindical
content:
A menudo, lograr una mejora en el contrato es solo la mitad de la batalla; la otra mitad consiste en hacer que se cumpla.

Fue una gran victoria en 2023 cuando nuestra campaña nacional por mejoras al contrato logró que la empresa de paquetería UPS eliminara su sistema de dos niveles salariales para los conductores. En el momento en que los conductores del nivel inferior ascendieron a la categoría regular, nuestro centro en Charleston, Carolina del Sur, contaba con 91 conductores de reparto a tiempo completo.

Sin embargo, con el paso del tiempo, algunos conductores se marcharon y la plantilla de nuestro centro se redujo a 75. Cuando solicitamos a la dirección que cubriera las vacantes, argumentaron que contábamos con personal suficiente.

Presentamos reclamaciones formales, pero fueron rechazadas porque no habíamos demostrado la necesidad de más personal. Así que decidimos demostrarlo.

La dirección cubría las carencias asignando parte de los repartos a miembros del sindicato con salarios más bajos, lo cual violaba nuestro contrato. Por ejemplo, los conductores de servicios aéreos solo deben entregar paquetes de envío aéreo. Por su parte, los conductores temporales —trabajadores de almacén a tiempo parcial que realizan algunos repartos solo deben utilizarse durante los meses de mayor actividad del año.

Presentamos quejas formales por casos en los que conductores de servicios aéreos entregaban paquetes de transporte terrestre, por conductores temporales que trabajaban fuera de temporada y por el traslado de conductores temporales de otros centros al nuestro, lo cual era una violación de las normas de antigüedad.

DIVIDE Y VENCERÁS

La dirección hizo todo lo posible por aplicar la táctica de "divide y vencerás". En las reuniones matutinas nos culpaban de que los conductores de la división aérea recibieran menos horas, y decían a nuestros compañeros repartidores que era culpa nuestra que ellos no "recibieran ayuda".

La empresa corregía temporalmente su comportamiento e intentaba echarnos la culpa de los problemas. Durante un tiempo, casi funcionó: ¡los afiliados sí nos culpaban a nosotros! Pero al cabo de unos días o una semana, todo volvía a la normalidad y los conductores se enfrentaban a los mismos problemas.

Empezamos a hablar con los conductores temporales y los de la división aérea, explicándoles que la verdadera solución era crear más puestos de trabajo permanentes a tiempo completo. Incluso cuando algunos conductores estaban enfadados con nosotros, seguíamos compartiendo información y hablando con ellos personalmente sobre cómo la empresa intentaba privarnos a todos de nuestro tiempo y nuestro trabajo.

Cada vez que descubrimos que los conductores de la división aérea habían entregado paquetes terrestres, nos asegurábamos de que cobraran la tarifa máxima de los conductores regulares, tal como exige el convenio. La diferencia podía ser de 15 dólares la hora o más, por lo que la empresa estaba robando a estos trabajadores al pagarles la tarifa más baja.

Cuando un conductor de la división aérea presentó su propia queja formal por primera vez, supimos que habíamos llegado a un punto de inflexión. Los afiliados empezaron a ver lo que estaba ocurriendo: la erosión de los buenos empleos sindicales. Con tiempo, otros empezaron a seguir su ejemplo.

Para entonces, ya había una docena de afiliados documentando las infracciones relacionadas con la división aérea y los conductores de tiempo parcial. Los afiliados nos avisaban cuando veían caras nuevas en el centro de trabajo y nosotros documentábamos la violación de las normas de antigüedad.

Un delegado sindical de un centro cercano —a quien habíamos conocido en un taller de Teamsters por un Sindicato Democratico— nos avisaba cuando la dirección enviaba a conductores de ruta de su centro a trabajar desde el nuestro.

Durante un año documentamos estas infracciones a diario, construyendo nuestro caso para demostrar la necesidad de más puestos de conductor a tiempo completo. Formamos un equipo de afiliados demostrándoles con hechos, más que con palabras, el principio de que "una agresión contra uno es una agresión contra todos".

PUNTO DE INFLEXIÓN

Mientras tanto, UPS había ofrecido un incentivo de 150.000 dólares a nivel nacional para animar a la gente a dejar la empresa. Antes de la temporada alta de vacaciones, se aprobaron las solicitudes de quienes habían pedido acogerse a estos incentivos y perdimos a varios conductores.

Esto supuso una mayor carga de trabajo …

author: Acratosaurio rex
title: El cabreo de Tomás Ibáñez
content:
Aquí el Tomás


Me apetecía decir algo sobre el artículo de Tomás Ibáñez de «

anarquismos en la encrucijada

», publicado por la prestigiosa web

acracia.org

 por dos motivos. El primero y principal, por el cabreo que tiene Tomás, porque le llaman anarquista de despacho, alejado de la realidad, que publica artículos académicos, que quita la ilusión por la revolución y cosas de esas… Tomás, tío, si a mí me echaran esos piropos estaría hasta contento. En mis andaduras por ahí me llaman

rata mercenaria bien pagá drogadicta fumada payasa ridícula que la historia me lo condenará cómo puedes ser tan imbécil hijo sin madre

,  por ejemplo, sin otro efecto que crearme una especie de risita nerviosa, tipo

jíiiiijijijijí

, y caminar por la calle girando continuamente para ver si me siguen.


El segundo que me gustaría comentar, es que mi tribuna es 

alasbarricadas.org

, que los anarquistas de bien saben que a pesar de su nombre, que suena a tambor de guerra y a muerte dolorosísima, está dirigido por la Amalia, que es una reformista más gorda que la Montseny. Y por lo tanto sus lectores son más bien ácratas incultos que desconocen quién es el Tomás, y que ni siquiera intuyen quién es Liza (¿Simpson? ¿Minelli?), Embat, y los plataformistas… Que son los antagonistas tomasianos. Como Lex Luthor con Spiderman. De esta manera, poniendo estos enlaces, con la esperanza de que los sigáis, culturizo a mis posibles lectores…


El rollo que se traen entre manos esos actores, es el del postmodernismo y lo de la revolución. Empecé a escuchar esa palabra (posmoderna) en los años ochenta, y desde entonces si me preguntan si lo soy, respondo… «

pos qué voy a sé, pos moelno joder

». Luego si me meto en los intríngulis, la verdad es que no entiendo ni papa de esa filosofía, así que corro un tupido velo y simplemente declaro que: Tomás, tío, no te cabrees, questoy contigo. Si hay que machacar cabezas, aquí me tienes.


No obstante añado que en pro de la objetividad, he intentado entender qué rayos es lo del anarquismo plataformista o especista o algo así… Me he leído sus análisis, y debo señalar, que en líneas generales, aunque –a diferencia de muchos textos posmodernos– se entiende lo que dicen, a los veinte párrafos de lectura, me entra un sueño invencible, incoercible, incontrolable. Lo de los

análisis certeros

, lo del

estudio de coyuntura

 o como diablos se diga, lo de la

recomposición de la vanguardia

… Me recuerda a los buenos viejos tiempos de los setenta y los sesenta, que te pillaba un maoísta y te sonaba una chapa mientras se sentaba en el autobús en tus rodillas, sin pedir permiso. No obstante, insto a los anarquistas a que lean cualquier cosa que caiga en sus manos, por si se les ilumina algo.


El tema de fondo es el de la revolución. Yo en eso soy clásico. La revolución, digan lo que digan, no se prepara: sucede. Y casi siempre los revolucionarios del Gran Día se encuentran montando algún comité o algún contubernio. Cuando me dicen que lo del 36, que se recuerdan sus noventa años, tuvo una preparación minuciosa, me pregunto… ¿Quién escribió el puñetero manual?¿Dónde estuvo la mente preclara colocando peones? ¿Por qué en Italia triunfó Mussolini, y no Durruti?


Algún día, llegaremos a saberlo. Actualmente, hacemos lo que podemos.


¡Por el comunismo trinitario! ¡Lo que es de uno es de todos, lo que es de todos es de nadie, lo que es de nadie es de uno!

author: CNT Iruña
title: Ciclo Cultural Popular de Agosto
content:
CNT Iruñea presenta para el mes de agosto un ciclo cultural popular, que constará de la proyección de varias obras de carácter cinematográfico, así como de un día de micrófono abierto. Los diferentes eventos se celebrarán en el local del sindicato e irán acompañados tanto de una introducción previa como de un coloquio posterior.

Bajo el nombre de Ciclo Cultural Popular, CNT Iruñea quiere ofrecer un espacio de cultura y ocio libre para todas aquellas personas de la clase trabajadora que se ven obligadas a permanecer en la ciudad durante el verano. Siguiendo la estela de ateneos libertarios, universidades populares y las diversas formas de difusión pedagógica de la tradición anarquista, CNT continúa, así, desarrollando los valores que, en cuanto institución de clase, se sostienen con quienes merecen el descanso y un lugar donde tomar un breve respiro para el intercambio de ideas antes de seguir con la lucha por la emancipación social.

Los eventos, fechas y horarios son los siguientes:

Sábado 1 · 11:30: Dellamorte Dellamore (Michele Soavi, 1994) · Película

Francesco Dellamorte es el cuidador del cementerio de Buffalora, un pueblo del norte de Italia. Dellamorte vive una vida solitaria apartado del mundo; su único amigo es Gnaghi, un pequeño, feo, lisiado y mudo compañero con el que comparte su ronda diaria por el cementerio. Desde hace algún tiempo, los muertos enterrados en el cementerio de Buffalora reviven debido a una súbita y misteriosa epidemia.

Miércoles 5 · 19:00: Italian Punk Hardcore 1980-1989 (Angelo Bitonto, Giorgio S. Senesi, Roberto Sivilia, 2015) Documental

Los orígenes del punk hardcore en Italia. Ciudades y centros neurálgicos. Autogestión, centros ocupados, política. Autoproducción, casetes de cinta y discos de vinilo. Los sellos independientes. Fanzines y boca a boca. Conciertos, manifestaciones, eventos. Los enfrentamientos, la violencia, los excesos, las drogas. La relación conflictiva entre el punk y la prensa, los periódicos y las revistas. El comienzo, el pico y el declive de las grandes bandas de los 80.

Sábado 8 · 11:30: Vivir la utopía (Juan A. Gamero, 1997) · Documental

La historia de movimiento anarcosindicalista en el Estado Español desde sus primeros atisbos, a finales del XIX, hasta el final de la guerra civil: la creación de la CNT y la FAI, el papel de la cultura y la educación con la Escuela Moderna, la explosión de ideas y la actividad que supuso la llegada de la II República, el golpe militar y, a la vez, la Revolución Social. Con el testimonio de hombres y mujeres anarquistas que vivieron aquella experiencia única.

Sábado 15 · 11:30: S lave to the Grind (Doug Robert Brown, 2018) · Documental

El grindcore es la música más intensa, agresiva y rápida del mundo. Al fusionar las actitudes anarquistas e izquierdistas de la escena punk del Reino Unido con la velocidad y la agresión ebria del death metal estadounidense, el grindcore continúa desafiando a la mayoría de los oyentes.

Miércoles 19 · 19:00: El tiempo de los obreros (Stan Neumann, 2020) · Documental

Serie de cuatro documentales independientes, encadenados cronológicamente, que repasa la historia de la clase trabajadora en Europa desde principios del siglo XVIII hasta la actualidad.

Miércoles 26 · 19:00: Micrófono abierto

Trae tu poesía, reflexiones, música (con tus instrumentos), monólogos, microrrelatos y cualquier forma de expresión que quieras compartir.

Sábado 29 · 11:30: Liberation Day (Ugis Olte, Morten Traavik, 2016) · Documental

Este documental musical sigue la increíble historia detrás del concierto en Pyongyang de la banda eslovena de música industrial Laibach para celebrar el Día de la Independencia de la hermética Corea del Norte.

La entrada Ciclo Cultural Popular de Agosto se publicó primero en Confederación Nacional del Trabajo .

author: Sarah Mahfouz, Sara Seif Eddin, Ehsan Salah, Hazem Tharwat, Mohamed Abdel Khaleq
title: The Damietta drone: A night of caution and speculation
content:
After a night of speculation, the Egyptian Cabinet said on Thursday morning that the fire that broke out aboard two energy vessels at Damietta Port the day before was caused by a drone strike, though it did not disclose who launched the drone.

A worker at the port who witnessed the incident says they heard a massive explosion at 2:10 pm on Wednesday. The blast occurred at berth 27, at the far end of the port near an area known as the silos zone, close to the facilities of SEGAS , the company that operates the Damietta liquefaction plant.

Police immediately sealed off the site and established a security cordon, the witness tells Mada Masr. “No extra security measures happened , and nobody had their phones taken. They cordoned off the berth. Ambulances arrived, but none left carrying casualties. They just closed off the area and we carried on with our workday as normal,” they say.

Two parliamentary sources speaking to Mada Masr confirm that the incident occurred at around 2:30 pm. Vessel traffic at the port was subsequently suspended until the affected ship had been towed out of the port basin. After 6 pm, navigation resumed, the sources say, which was confirmed by the Damietta Port Authority in a statement on Thursday.

The vessel targeted was the Energos Winter , a floating liquified natural gas regasification unit owned by the American New Fortress Energy. Last summer, the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company signed a five-year agreement with the company for hiring the vessel.

A second vessel nearby was also seen aflame.

A source at the Petroleum Ministry says the Energos Winter had been operating at full capacity, supplying between 400 million and 500 million cubic feet of natural gas per day to the national grid — around six percent of Egypt’s peak summer demand of 7.5 billion cubic feet daily. It was one of four regasification vessels on which the country currently relies.

The vessel has now been taken out of service and is not expected to return anytime soon, the source says. It will leave Egypt for maintenance and repairs for the damage sustained in the strike.

As an interim measure, the source says Egypt will rely on the Energos Force , a regasification vessel stationed at Aqaba. Under an agreement reached with Jordan in late 2024 , Egypt can draw on part of the vessel’s operating capacity in emergencies, i n addition to increasing the use of Mazut to meet any energy interruption .

Thursday’s government statement confirmed what has been already circulated by international media outlets the day of the strike: that the fire was caused by a drone strike. The first official statement, issued on Wednesday by the Petroleum Ministry, had referred only to the fire, without mentioning its cause or denying the international press reports.

From the outset, Egyptian state institutions were intent on carefully controlling media coverage of the incident. Egyptian newspapers took down a report quoting TV host and MP Mostafa Bakry, who had cited what he described as “security sources” denying that the fire had resulted from a drone attack. The report was removed within minutes of publication.

That approach was clearly reflected in the following day’s press coverage, with most outlets making no mention of the incident. The few that did cover it merely carried the Petroleum Ministry’s statement briefly and on an inside page.

But as maritime security firms, including Ambrey and Vanguard, publicly said that a drone strike had caused the fire, the government decided to reveal that detail itself, while stressing that “no party has claimed responsibility for the incident.”

A senior Cabinet source says that the Petroleum Ministry’s Wednesday statement was issued at the direct instruction of the presidency, with orders for its immediate release before anyone else could comment. The government later received instructions to disclose that a drone had been involved, which it did in Thursday morning’s statement, the source adds.

One of the parliamentary sources says Thursday’s statement most likely came after authorities realized the matter can no longer be concealed. “The international press is talking. There are satellites. It can’t stay hidden,” they say.

According to the second parliamentary source, US President Donald Trump’s remarks on Wednesday that he had been briefed on the incident left the government no choice but to reveal and explain what had happened.

author: Gaurav Kumar
title: What India’s Cockroach Party won — and what’s next
content:
This article What India’s Cockroach Party won — and what’s next was originally published by Waging Nonviolence .

Thirty-six days after a joke about “cockroaches” became a youth movement, India’s education minister was gone. On July 25, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned after weeks of protests over failures in the public examination system and demands for political accountability. The Cockroach Janta Party, or CJP, declared victory — “Cockroaches won. Democracy won.”

For a movement that began online in May and grown into a nationwide agitation, forcing a cabinet minister from office was an unmistakable political concession. But almost as soon as the protesters packed up, the meaning of that victory became less certain.

Three days later, the movement was already threatening to return to the streets. The CJP said over 100 protesters been arrested nationwide, with cases filed in the states of Delhi, Assam, West Bengal and Bihar, despite assurances that demonstrators would not face punitive action. CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka warned that the agitation could resume if those arrested were not released.

Bihar police announced that the protesters had been released and would face no adverse legal action. But the assurance did not hold in other states , like West Bengal and Assam, where more than a dozen are still being detained.

Removing a minister was a visible symbol of accountability; ensuring that other promises made to end the protests were actually honored would require something harder — sustained organization after the crowds had gone home.

A movement that couldn’t be decapitated

When Delhi last saw a mass youth mobilization, over the citizenship law in 2020 , the state answered by naming the organizers in a conspiracy chargesheet: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have now been held for more than five years under India’s 1967 anti-terror law and were refused bail again on July 4 , 16 days before the cockroaches marched on Parliament.

It began as a joke. Amidst a youth uproar over invalidated examination results, during which India’s highest judge referred to the nation’s youth as “cockroaches,” a Boston-based student from India, Abhijeet Dipke, posted on X, “What if the cockroaches marched?”

The strategic satire of India’s Gen Z ‘Cockroach’ movement

The joke carried a serious message: The protesters who turned out in response, under the banner of the Cockroach Janta Party, saw themselves as people the political system had stopped listening to.

But the Cockroach Janta Party — a parody of the Bharatiya Janata Party, or BJP, the Hindu right-wing party that has governed India since 2014 — had few of the trappings of a serious political party. There was a website where people could sign up; there was an Instagram account that had grown rapidly; and there was Dipke. By July, he was leading the sit-ins and the marches from a stage in Central Delhi — a founder the movement had acquired without ever electing one, and who insisted, along with everybody else there, that the CJP had no leader.

For five weeks, Delhi Police dealt with a protest that offered nothing conventional to target. There was no office to raid and no membership list to seize — the two things that allowed police to quell earlier movements.

So on the morning of July 18, police went for the one man everyone knew.

Sonam Wangchuk, an engineer and education reformer from the Indian Himalayas, is 59 years old and was 20 days into a hunger strike. He had lost more than 18 pounds. Police carried him from the protest site and took him to hospital.

Wangchuk had become the most recognizable face in a movement that insisted it had no leader. He runs a school in the region of Ladakh for children who struggle in India’s examination system and is a recipient of the Ramon Magsaysay Award, often described as Asia’s Nobel.

Delhi Police said they acted on a High Court order and medical advice. Protesters tried to stop officers from taking Wangchuk away, leading to what police described as a “slight commotion.”

But the police statement did not end with Wangchuk’s health. It also asked the remaining protesters to leave. They did not.

Taking a man 20 days into a hunger strike to a hospital could be explained as a medical decision. Asking everyone else to clear the square was something different.

By that afternoon the square was fuller than it had been all month, with people packed under sheets of black plastic strung between trees, facing a stage with nobody on it …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Report from Springfield, Ohio: Haitians Brace for ICE Crackdown After TPS Protections End
content: The Haitian community is bracing for mass deportations after the Supreme Court last month sided with the Trump administration to end TPS , or Temporary Protected Status, for over 300,000 Haitians as well as thousands of Syrians who fled violence in their home countries. According to an internal government document, the plans to round up and deport Haitian immigrants could start this week. President Trump has long expressed animus toward Haitians in the United States. During the 2024 presidential campaign, he amplified false claims that Haitians in Springfield, Ohio, were eating cats and dogs. “The fear is so huge in our community,” says Vilès Dorsainvil, co-founder and executive director of the Haitian Support Center in Springfield, Ohio. Due to the risk of violence in Haiti, the U.S. government is warning American citizens not to travel to the country. For many Haitian immigrants who fled to the U.S. for safety, “they do not have a country to go back to.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Citizens Bank Cuts Ties to ICE Prison Companies GEO Group & CoreCivic After Grassroots De-ICE Campaign
content:
A coalition of social justice organizations is celebrating a recent decision by Citizens Bank to divest from private prison companies that operate immigration jails for the federal government. The financial institution has faced significant pressure from protesters for providing more than $2.5 billion in financing to CoreCivic and the GEO Group, which work directly with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. While the bank denied that activist pressure affected its decision, the De- ICE Citizens Bank Coalition counted it as a victory.

“It was absolutely thanks to the incredible work of the activists,” says Jake Ephros, a Democratic Socialist member of Jersey City Council, who helped push the municipality to pull over $200 million in city funds from the bank.

We also speak with Rev. John Edgerton, senior minister of Old South Church in Boston and a board member of the Greater Boston Interfaith Organization. He credits “a broad movement” with the victory. “The pressure became too much for Citizens to bear, and they had to do the right thing.”

author: Kamau Wairuri
title: Reflections on the Financialization of Politics in Africa
content:
In mid-July, I participated in the Conference on the Financialization of Politics in Africa that was held in Accra, Ghana. The conference brought together various stakeholders from the continent, with representatives from the African Union, governments, civil society, and development partners. The conference was organized by the Community of Practice on Money in Politics with the support of the Centre for Democratic Development in Ghana (CDD-Ghana), the Open Society Foundations (OSF), and the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC). The aim of both the Community of Practice and the conference was to begin structuring meaningful engagement between stakeholders who are committed to deepening democracy and integrity in Africa by curtailing the growing influence of money in politics.

The conference succeeded in developing a strongly shared understanding of the nature and extent of the problem at hand with respect to the increasingly central role that finance is playing in African politics, both within and outside electoral seasons. During elections, it is widely understood that money plays an important role in determining who makes it to the ballot and, more often than not, how they fare in the election. A series of studies by the Westminster Foundation for Democracy (WFD) and their partners have shown how expensive it is for people to run for office in Africa. Their latest studies, conducted in 2020 and 2021, found that it costs an average of US$68,215 for a parliamentary seat in Ghana and US$182,000 in Kenya. These are high figures that end up excluding from political competition people with limited access to finance, especially women and youth. Hence, it is often noted that many of the young people and women who get into politics often rely on sponsors and godfathers. Of course, some are independently wealthy, which often raises speculation about the source of their wealth. These are important issues to engage with and address with respect to the exclusionary nature of expensive elections, not just for women and youth, but also for other marginalized groups.

Vote buying

One issue that seems to have occupied much of our attention is the question of vote buying. It is often believed that most of the money that is spent in politics goes towards voter bribery. As the argument goes, vote buying is a problem because it distorts political choices and is therefore a major threat to democracy. A lot of work and investment by democracy promoters have gone into this area, piquing the interest of my friend and colleague Dr Sae’ed Husaini. Writing based on an ethnographic, comparative study of four different locations in Nigeria, he argues that this focus may be misplaced. He finds that vote buying is neither as prevalent nor as effective as the focus we place on it suggests. That is, most people do not actually receive the money that is supposedly distributed by politicians and many of those who receive it believe that they are free to make their choices independent of these inducements.

There are many potential case studies to look at, but Kenya presents some interesting recent examples that offer great fodder for analysis. In the recent by-election in Ol Kalou, the ruling party invested heavily in inducements to voters and still lost embarrassingly. Even noting that by-elections are quite different from general elections, we can examine how the money was flowing to get a more refined sense of the extent of the distribution of funds and also explore why it was not effective in swaying the voter to support the incumbent government.

However, leaving voter suppression aside for now, we must also compare this with the preceding by-elections, such as in Mbeere North where, with heavy inducements during the campaign, the ruling party emerged victorious. Such an analysis would help us obtain a richer view that will further enhance our understanding of this phenomenon. Similar studies across other African countries may help to build a strong body of evidence that would challenge prevailing orthodoxy and perhaps allow for more room to engage on other questions on the impact of financialization on politics and policy.

Looking beyond elections

It is an issue of concern that the conversation on the financialization of politics often focuses on elections, with less attention being paid to how money is also a tool for purchasing policy outcomes in the period between elections. It is true that financiers invest in …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Tierra y dignidad: luchas ancestrales, voces de futuro
content:
Por Darío Aranda

Desde Eldorado hasta Esquel. De Las Lomitas a Loncopué. De Andalgalá a Guadalupe Norte. Son personas que no aparecen en redes digitales ni en grandes medios de comunicación. No aspiran al “éxito” que ofrece el sistema ni se acercan al poder de turno. Participan de espacios colectivos que priorizan el cuidado del agua, el aire, el territorio, la vida. Y están empecinadas en construir alternativas al capitalismo que depreda la tierra. Son familias campesinas, pueblos indígenas, organizaciones de base y asambleas socioambientales.

Desde hace décadas afirman que el modelo de país –a base de agronegocio, petróleo, minería, forestales, megarepresas y energía nuclear– es un nuevo capítulo de los espejitos de colores que lleva 500 años, una trampa no solo económica, sino (y sobre todo) política, con amplias consecuencias sociales,ambientales y sanitarias.

Un modelo extractivo que fue (y es) piedra basal de todos los gobiernos. Protagonizado por grandes empresas y presidentes, gobernadores, legisladores e intendentes, jueces y fiscales, que no aceptan alternativas a la de exprimir territorios y vidas. “ Los supuestos representantes del pueblo no son gobernantes , son gerentes ejecutores de las grandes empresas y de los terratenientes”, denuncia Marcos Pastrana, abuelo diaguita de Tafí del Valle (Tucumán).

Las pruebas, voces y estudios de las consecuencias del modelo extractivo son contundentes. Solo a modo de ejemplo: la concentración de la tierra se supera año a año. El 1 por ciento de las explotaciones agropecuarias controla el 36 por ciento de la tierra; y el 55 por ciento de las chacras (las más pequeñas) cuenta con solo el 2 por ciento de la tierra. Argentina experimenta una reforma agraria pero al revés, donde muy pocos tienen casi todo, y muchos no tienen casi nada. Las zonas de megaminería, como Andalgalá y Jáchal, son de las regiones más pobres del país. En las localidades donde se explota Vaca Muerta, “las mayores reservas” de hidrocarburos no convencionales, no hay gas natural para la población y hasta se siguen calefaccionando con leña. En Añelo, epicentro petrolero, existen más prostíbulos que escuelas: es el “desarrollo” que brinda el extractivismo.

Las enfermedades asociadas al uso de agrotóxicos aumentaron exponencialmente en las regiones del agronegocio. “Epidemia de cáncer en zonas sojeras” , denuncian los pueblos fumigados, desde Avia Terai (Chaco) a Exaltación de la Cruz (Buenos Aires), desde Ituzaingó Anexo (Córdoba) a San Jorge (Santa Fe). Desastre sanitario también confirmado con cientos de estudios científicos. “Es un experimento masivo a cielo abierto”, había alertado el científico Andrés Carrasco en 2009.

En un país donde las pruebas son irrefutables, igual se reproducen discursos mediáticos, desde grandes medios de comunicación hasta los inefables “influencers”, que llaman a explotar la naturaleza o, en el mejor de los casos, a hacerlo con “cuidado”, como si se pudiera desmontar millones de hectáreas o detonar montañas de forma “sustentable”.

Cuando la realidad está alterada de forma extrema es necesario buscar otras categorías de análisis para poder pensar el presente, luego accionar y transformar la realidad. Con una pobreza del 50 por ciento, con un millón de niños que no pueden cenar cada noche (datos de Unicef), con jubilaciones que condenan a la miseria y una política que, con complicidad judicial, arrasa territorios, no alcanza con decir que se trata solo de un modelo económico. Otra categoría posible para pensar la realidad: “Nos han declarado la guerra”, explicaron en numerosas oportunidades los zapatistas, en referencia a las políticas económicas, sociales y represivas que padecen.

Es explícito el desprecio, la crueldad y el cinismo del poder, la violencia de los de arriba contra los de abajo.

El lonko mapuche Mauro Millán resumió la situación actual: “Nuestra lucha es por la existencia misma de nuestros pueblos”. Desde hace años que en Catamarca y San Juan se denuncia la “dictadura minera”, donde las asambleas plantean con claros ejemplos cómo las multinacionales extractivas manejan a su antojo a gobernadores, legisladores y al Poder Judicial.

A quienes viven en ciudades, y a quienes no salen de la realpolitik (esa forma de actuar, con más pragmatismo que coherencia ideológica) ni traspasan la Avenida General Paz, les parece exagerado hablar de “dictaduras mineras” y de “guerras” por la vida. author: J.E.
title: OCD and the Anxiety/Gut Connection
content:
H ello, my name is J.E. I’m almost 50 years old and I have struggled with OCD since around the age of nine, and I have also been diagnosed with C-PTSD.

My first memory of OCD symptoms, at the age of nine, was a painful memory about how we moved into this apartment after losing my mother. I specifically remember not being able to walk barefoot on the carpet in our apartment. Before losing my mother, we had always lived in brand-new, very clean homes, and this apartment had old, stained carpet. It terrified me. I couldn’t stand the way my feet felt “contaminated” from the dirty carpet. The work I would do to avoid it was incredible, and a foreshadowing into how I would react to so many things in life, not just dirty carpet.

Much later, I learned more about OCD themes and how contamination works, etc. It’s interesting because over time, as I would “overcome” one contamination or compulsion, a new one would develop. I learned in an OCD support group that OCD really attacks the things you care deeply about. So as my knowledge changed, or my awareness about how germs worked versus how chemicals were bad and how that worked, there was a shift in my OCD symptoms.

For example, I lived with a boyfriend for seven years, and during that time he would install cable in people’s homes for a living, which involved him crawling around in people’s attics. He didn’t shower when he got home, and I felt itchy after hugging him. And that’s when I developed one of my biggest OCD compulsions. Later, as I look back on the experience, I see how being itchy from exposure to insulation was a very real thing, how my ex was simply an asshole for not showering, and how my brain developed ways to protect me. It went into hyper-overdrive, thinking it would keep me safe. I believe the need for safety was the overall drive that took over when my mom left.

A little over ten years ago, I remember lying in bed paralyzed from pain I was feeling in my abdomen. I looked down and I could see a visible, misshapen bulge; it almost seemed to move, even. I scheduled the necessary medical appointments to get checked out. An ultrasound was performed, and I was diagnosed with a uterine fibroid. Since I had previously had surgery to have my tubes tied (to get off the birth control I had been taking for over five years), I think the decision to remove my uterus and fibroid was simple. Get it out. I was on board entirely, thinking my symptoms of excruciating pain would finally be resolved. I had the surgery. Notice how they call this particular surgical procedure “hysterectomy”? It’s the hysteria part of the word I have a problem with. I always say that I had my uterus removed to avoid using the term altogether.

After surgery, when the doctor came to talk to me, he described what he diagnosed as endometriosis that he scraped out of my abdomen. I had never heard of the condition, but later, when I researched more, came to find out it is one of the most painful conditions a person can have. He also said, “You definitely want to get your colon checked out.” It literally took me about eight years to find out what he really meant by that statement!

People talk about the mind-body connection. People talk about gut healing. So many clues along the way, but until very recently, I never made the direct connection between my gut and how anxiety created physical problems! Why did not one single medical professional tell me this information? Why did it take so many trial and errors, constant medical appointments where everything “checked out fine” but I was struggling so much with my health, and getting zero answers from the medical profession we’ve been so accustomed to trusting? Why did it take a major surgery, taking out an organ unrelated to my gut, and eight years of trial and error to discover this information on my own?

Along my path of stumbling and grasping for answers, I wound up in the emergency room, convinced I was in danger of my appendix rupturing. I could barely walk, I was in so much pain. They took me back to the treatment room, got an IV set up in my arm in case they needed to do emergency surgery, and did a CT scan. Then the results came back. I remember the look on the doctor’s face as they were reading the report. Like they couldn’t believe what they were seeing. Of course they used different language, but basically I was told, “You’re full of shit.” Literally, my body had accumulated so much old waste, old poop that my colon and large intestine were …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: De qué hablamos cuando hablamos de tierra en Argentina
content:
El Gobierno impulsa el proyecto de Ley de "Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada", que en la práctica es una reforma a la Ley de Tierras. Promueve la extranjerización de la tierra en Argentina y facilita los desalojos a las comunidades indígenas y campesinas. Se prevé que el tratamiento en el Senado sea el jueves 6 de agosto y las organizaciones campesinas y socioambientales convocan a una movilización al Congreso para ese día. El Observatorio de Tierras, del Conicet y la Universidad de Buenos Aires, califica la iniciativa como “una contrarreforma a favor del capital”. La Mesa Agroalimentaria Argentina, que nuclea a organizaciones de productores campesinos e indígenas, manifestó su rechazo. Actualmente, 13 millones de hectáreas están en manos de empresarios extranjeros.

A partir de 2008, tras la crisis financiera global, la tierra pasó a ser un commodity a nivel global para los capitales especulativos. La Ley de Tierras, sancionada en 2011, estableció límites para la extranjerización. Según la normativa actual, personas físicas o jurídicas no pueden comprar más del 15 por ciento de las tierras rurales en el territorio nacional. La Ley de Tierras establece también que dicho porcentaje se computará para las superficies provinciales y municipales. Y existe un tope de 1.000 hectáreas en la zona núcleo de la producción agropecuaria para un mismo titular extranjero.

En esa ley no se consideró extranjero solo al titular de la propiedad, sino que se consideró foráneas a las empresas controladas por hasta un 25 por ciento de personas físicas o jurídicas extranjeras. Pero el gobierno de Mauricio Macri, mediante el Decreto 820/2016, elevó ese tope a más del 51 por ciento.

Con estos antecedentes, el proyecto impulsado por La Libertad Avanza y negociado por Patricia Bullrich en el Congreso con sus liados provinciales, propone:

Eliminar los límites de compra de tierras rurales por parte de empresarios o compañías extranjeras.

Suprimir la restricción de compra de más de 1.000 hectáreas a empresarios foráneos en la zona núcleo de la producción agropecuaria.

Dejar sin efecto la prohibición de adquirir tierras ribereñas de cursos de agua permanente o en zonas de frontera.

Eliminar el Consejo Interministerial de Tierras Rurales. Es el ente encargado de regular lo que ocurre con las tierras a nivel nacional y de supervisar que se cumplan los límites de adquisición de tierras rurales.

Modificar el concepto de “titularidad extranjera” y habilitar a comprar tierras en el país a cualquier persona física extranjera (no radicada en el país) y a personas jurídicas con participación de capitales internacionales. Es decir, un fondo de inversión privado de Arabia Saudita, Vanguard, BlackRock o cualquier corporación transnacional podría adquirir tierra sin límites.

Introducir el juicio sumarísimo (procesos breves para resolver situaciones urgentes) para habilitar desalojos en zonas urbanas y rurales. Habilita el uso de la fuerza pública para esos operativos.

Mantener las prohibiciones vigentes para los Estados extranjeros y empresas estatales extranjeras.

Delegar a las provincias la decisión de qué tierras vender o la capacidad de crear legislaciones específicas de protección (argumento de “dominio originario” que ya se utilizó para desarmar la Ley de Glaciares).

Derogar el artículo 4 del Decreto 15.385 de 1944, que establece: “Declárase de conveniencia nacional que los bienes ubicados en las zonas de seguridad pertenezcan a ciudadanos argentinos nativos”. Por zonas de seguridad para la defensa nacional se entienden, por ejemplo, las zonas de frontera.

Limitar la capacidad del Estado para expropiar tierras de “utilidad pública” (con modificaciones a la Ley 21.499 sobre Expropiaciones y Ley 24.374 sobre Regularización Dominial).

La reforma alcanza también la Ley de Manejo del Fuego. La prohibición de cambiar el uso del suelo tras un incendio quedaría restringida a bosques nativos definidos por ley, eliminando las salvaguardas sobre humedales, pastizales, matorrales y áreas agrícolas.

Este proyecto acentuará la extranjerización de la tierra rural en Argentina. En el país hay, según el Observatorio de Tierras, más de 13 millones de hectáreas extranjerizadas que se concentran mayoritariamente en zonas estratégicas. Por ejemplo: en áreas de frontera, a la vera del río Paraná, en nodos logísticos clave, en regiones con potencial minero, en territorios con cursos de agua en zonas frías, en acuíferos de importancia estratégica y en …

author: Unknown
title: Ursula K. Le Guin - The Shobies’ Story
content:
Author

: Ursula K. Le Guin

Title

: The Shobies’ Story

Date

: April 1990


Foreword


 In my crustier moments I’ve been known to assert that, while science fiction boasts any number of enthralling yarn spinners, brilliant visionaries, and witty satirists, it has produced only one wholly literary voice. That’s not true, of course. It’s certainly not fair to Samuel R. Delany, Thomas Disch, Lucius Shepard, Karen Joy Fowler, Judith Moffet, Michael Bishop, and perhaps a dozen others. And yet if SFWA ever got itself into a literary jousting tournament with some rival guild, the prize being a government grant or a small planet or a subscription to The New Yorker or something, there’s no question whom I’d want to send onto the field.


 Ursula K. Le Guin received the National Book Award for The Farthest Shore, the third novel in the Earthsea cycle, as well as a Hugo and a Nebula for The Left Hand of Darkness and the same pair of trophies for The Dispossessed. This volume celebrates her most recent literary honor—a Nebula for Tehanu: The Last Book of Earthsea—by offering up another Le Guin work from the final ballot, a complex and audacious novelette called “The Shobies’ Story.”


 Even if Tehanu had not taken the top prize, I would have accorded “The Shobies’ Story” a prime spot in this volume, for I believe that—through its marvelous conceit of “churten” travel— it raises crucial questions about social hierarchies, interspecies bonding, and the consensus model of reality. Le Guin aficionados will quickly notice that it belongs to the “Hainish League” saga, her ongoing narrative of galactic exploration.


 “This story grew out of an idea I have been chewing on for years about the importance of story, of narrative,” Le Guin reports. “Speaking not metaphorically but fairly literally, it seems that people who can see their life as a story, with a ‘plot’ or at least narrative continuity (possibly even a happy ending), get along okay, while people who lose that narrative sense are in a lot of trouble, maybe to the point of psychopathy. I’m not talking about personal control, being the ‘author of your fate,’ because in cultures where individuals don’t control their lives much at all, people can be totally content with the cultural narrative, and live it beautifully. Even if the story itself is stupid or psychopathic, like the war story or the white-supremacy story, if we believe in it and it makes some sense to us we get along, we stay alive, we even think we know what we’re doing.


 “Well, then, the idea of using narrative as a means of travel is really just an extension of this basic idea of narrative as means of existence. So the Shobies showed up and started telling their story. Their stories. Of course they were science fiction stories, what else?”


The Shobies’ Story


 They met at the Port more than a month before their first flight together, and there, calling themselves after their ship as most crews did, became the Shobies. Their first consensual decision was to spend their isyeye in the coastal village of Liden, on Hain, where the negative ions could do their thing.


 Liden was a fishing port with an eighty-thousand-year history and a population of four hundred. Its fisherfolk farmed the rich shoal waters of their bay, shipped the catch inland to the cities, and managed the Liden Resort for vacationers and tourists and new space crews on isyeye (the word is Hainish and means “making a beginning together,” or “beginning to be together,” or, used technically, “the period of time and area of space in which a group forms if it is going to form.” A honeymoon is an isyeye of two). The fisherwomen and fishermen of Liden were as weathered as driftwood and about as talkative. Six-year-old Asten, who had misunderstood slightly, asked one of them if they were all eighty thousand years old. “Nope,” she said.


 Like most crews, the Shobies used Hainish as their common language. So the name of the one Hainish crew member, Sweet Today, carried its meaning as words as well as name, and at first seemed a silly thing to call a big, tall, heavy woman in her late fifties, imposing of carriage and almost as taciturn as the villagers. But her reserve proved to be a deep well of congeniality and tact, to be called upon as needed, and her name soon began to sound quite right. She had family—all Hainish have family—kinfolk of all denominations, grandchildren and cross-cousins, affines and cosines, scattered all over the Ekumen, but no …

author: anarchy
title: Remembering Murray Bookchin
content:
Murray Bookchin was one of the most relevant voices in the ecological debate all throughout the second half of the 20th century, combining deep philosophical, anthropological and historical knowledge on the one hand, and some brilliant political insights on the other hand. His intellectual biography is a complex one, merging intellectual and militant engagement, and ranging from syndicalism to Trotskyism, and later anarchism. Importantly, he developed the concept of social ecology, for which he is best known. The many polemics in which he was involved made him a controversial figure in the anarchist movement, but the relevance and originality of his contributions are out of question.

From Marxism via anarchism to communalism

Murray Bookchin’s political engagement starts at a very young age, under the influence of the socialist ideas that his grandmother taught him since he was a kid. As a 15-year-old, he tried to enlist for the Spanish Civil War and got refused because of his young age. As a young factory worker, he was engaged in syndicalist struggles, and broke with his Stalinist political affiliation before turning 20. He embraced Trotskyist ideas and joined the Socialist Workers Party and the United Electrical Workers while working at General Motors. In the early ‘50s, he started to get interested in ecological issues and wrote his first essays under the pseudonym Lewis Herber in order to avoid McCarthyistic repression. At the end of the 1950s, he considered himself an anarchist, and a few months earlier than Rachel Carson’s seminal work Silent Spring, he published Our Synthetic Environment. During his anarchist years, he developed the concept of social ecology, which would shape his thinking for the rest of his life. He broke with anarchism during the 1990s because of what he considered a primitivist, individualistic turn in the movement – a critique that is addressed in his 1995 book Social anarchism or Lifestyle anarchism . In his late years, he coined the notion of communalism, that can be considered his last intellectual and political turn.

Social ecology and post-scarcity

Bookchin’s main theoretical contribution to ecological thinking is undoubtedly the notion of social ecology. In a time when the deep ecology movement was dominant in the USA, Bookchin proposed an idea of ecology centred on social critique, arguing that domination over nature is a result of social hierarchies, and that in order to overcome the former, we need to uproot the very basis of social domination. If it does not comprehend social critique, ecology is just a moral concern at best, and a collection of “green” technologies that perpetuate oppression. Ecology is social in that it needs to address the way in which society (or second nature) is the outcome of natural evolutionary development (or first nature). This makes it possible for him to maintain that all forms of societal relation to nature are in fact political. Every human society is always situated in the context of an eco-community that encompasses non-human life as well as inorganic systems that support life.

Bookchin thought that an ecological society and politics should ground in cooperation and mutualism its actions, because mutual aid and solidarity are not simply ethical values, but they are also the best evolutionary strategy. In this sense, he followed a path that was well outlined by Élisée Reclus and Peter Kropotkin. According to Bookchin, nature provides us with enough resources and with an outstanding rationality that makes us capable of developing ecological technologies that would allow everyone to live a dignified life, one that is free from the production of needs and can focus instead on liberated desire. This thesis is at the heart of his notion of post-scarcity – a notion that he links to anarchism and ecology in the book Post-scarcity anarchism. The alternative we are facing, he says, is no longer socialism or barbarism; it is rather anarchism or annihilation.

Libertarian municipalism and the Rojava struggle

The politics of social ecology is libertarian municipalism, a form of stateless politics based on decentralisation, direct democracy and a general rethinking of urbanisation and of the organisation of work. Bookchin’s views on such themes lead him to argue not only for decentralization at an institutional level – which is nonetheless one important tenet of libertarian municipalism – but also on a geographical level, maintaining that large cities …

author: Unknown
title: Tidningen Brand - Till Alfred Stern
content:
Författare

: Tidningen Brand

Titel

: Till Alfred Stern

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #13 1917


 Högt gick stridens vågor där nere i den skånska metropolen. Förbittrad var kampen mellan Kung Grotte och hans trälande slavar. Barn kvedo och kvinnor svulto tysta i eländets bakgårdar. Striden började bli ojämn. Grotte kallade köpta män att falla de upproriska trälarna i ryggen och svälten skar allt djupare i de utmärglade benraderna. Förtvivlan var nära.


 Det var då tre unga män högburet satte in sina liv i kampen.


 Vad värde har livet? Just så stort värde man själv sätter på det. Och de tre unga männen älskade att leva, att

'leva i kamp för rättfärdighet och frihet.** Och

därför satsade de livet,

 som insats i kampen.


 De mäktiga kastade dem i fängelse, och det fanns män, som skulle vara talesmän för arbetarnas egen klass, som ksatade smuts på deras gärning, kastade smuts till dem bak fängelsets galler.


 I snart nio långa och tunga lidandets år ha ni suttit bak den kapitalistiska "rättvisans" starksmidda lås. Äntligen började arbetes slavar, vars djupa sympatier ni dock alltid haft, att otåligt banka på fängelseportarna.


 "Släpp ut våra lidande kamrater!"


 Den kapitalistiska "rättvisans" lakejer visste icke vad, men de kände förbrytelsen växa bland massorna över edert martyrium, och försiktigt gläntade de en smula på dörren och släppte

ut dig, kamrat!


 Välkommen till friheten och livet!


 Vi vet icke mycket om dig nu, vet icke ens om du är med i revolutionens idéer, eller om de tunga fängelseåren ha gjort ditt sinne dystert och trött. Men ett veta vi: att du offrade dig elt och med fritt sinne för den stora kampen, att du lidit nio långa års tunga kval i ofrihet, i andlig avspärrning, i brutal undertryckelse. Och ett veta vi, att vi älskar dig för det offer du bragt, att vi glädjas med dig över den återvunna friheten, det återvunna livet.


 Så var hälsad kamrat! Tag din plats i ledet om du har kraft till det. Eller tig om du vill det. Vi skola icke lasta dig. Du har gjort din värnplikt i den sociala revolutionens tjänst, och vi kunna endast önska att tusenden voro så offervilliga som du! Då skulle segern icke vara långt borta.


 Och låt oss så hoppas att dina och våra ännu inspärrade kamrater snart också måtte vara mitt ibland oss.


Brand.

author: Unknown
title: Victor Arendorff - Välkommen till friheten!
content:
Författare

: Victor Arendorff

Titel

: Välkommen till friheten!

Undertitel

: Alfred Stern tillägnad

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #13 1917


 Frihetslängtan, den har starka vingar

 Ingen boja har den kraft, som tvingar

 dem, när de till flykt sig breda ut.

 Frihetshjälten skrämmer intet galler.

 Han står säker, han, och icke faller,

 om ock fångenskapen ej har slut.


 Våra rop om frihet ändå väckte

 dem, som makten ha, och äntligt bräckte

 cellens gallerjärn och tunga dörr. -

 Långa år därinom du fått lida,

 men välkommen nu till oss, som strida

 samma hårda bittra kamp som förr.


 Minns du... minns du dina ungdomsdrömmar?

 Brusar än ditt blod i heta strömmar

 för din ungdoms vackra ideal?

 Icke drömma blott - du kunde handla,

 ville dröm till värklighet förvandla,

 men din lön blev cellens mörka kval.


 Mången vårsols glada gyllenskimmer

 du sett strimma celldörrns grova timmer...

 I förtvivlan då du sjunkit hop.

 I förbittring knöt du dina händer

 och du grät med sammanbitna tänder.

 Ingen hörde dina klagorop.


 Jo, vi hörde dem, och starkt vi höjde

 rop på frihet, som omsider böjde

 cellens galler för din längtans blick.

 Hur i ängslan vi kamrater levde!

 Ack, vi ropade, och ropet krävde

 nyckeln blott, som till din frihet gick!


 Du är fri och vårens solljusglitter

 hälsar dig med sparvare jubelkvitter,

 som i cellens pina du väl glömt.

 Du är vårens barn och vårens ljusning

 ligger än i dina drömmars tjusning -

 samma röda dröm, din ungdom drömt!

author: Kevin Carson
title: A Half-Built Garden, by Ruthanna Emrys (Tor 2022)
content:
A Half-Built Garden is a well thought out first contact story, with an engaging plot — things which would make it well worth reading on its own. But as anyone familiar with my previous reviews will be aware, when I review near-future sci-fi stories about liberatory postcapitalist utopias, that’s not my primary concern. I review them for their future history worldbuilding — a sin comparable to Auden’s reading the Bible for its prose.

The story is set in the 2080s, following a mid-century Time of Troubles, when the world is emerging from the ruins of capitalism and creating a new, humanly tolerable society.

The dominant governing institution is the watershed network, a federation of self-managed local institutions more or less equivalent to bioregions, which incorporates most of the world’s population and resources. The balance of power is the result of a mostly non-violent mid-century revolution beginning a generation or two earlier, in which a combination of boycotts, sabotage, and other direct action forced the corporations into offshore enclaves. The viewpoint character, who inhabits the Chesapeake Watershed, reminisces about the days when her parents “helped place the first illicit sensors in the Potomac and barricaded factories to enforce the first crowdsourced decisions of the nascent Dandelion Revolution.”

The corporations, as is typical for this genre, consist of “billionaire lords and serf-employees huddled behind their fencelines on their artificial islands.” Their inhabitants, aside from “a few converts and visitors,” are “only the descendants of the people who’d arrived with their founder — allies and employees who’d prioritized fleeing apocalypse over creating community to stop it.”

Corporate enclaves were bounded by “fencelines,” apparently imposed from outside by the networks during the course of the Dandelion Revolution. “As for the corporations, eventually we didn’t allow it. People like my parents organized to stop them, and created the first watershed networks.” Actions taken during the Revolution ranged from “setting limits on their carbon production to get warming under control, to blocking their shipping if they went over their carbon budgets.” The corporations, “which couldn’t bear the transformation, …eventually… barricaded themselves behind their own fencelines on a few artificial islands….”

The corporations, since their relegation to island enclaves, have mostly refused any official recognition of the watersheds’ existence, and for their own part “lost any legal existence outside their own territory a long time ago.” They send observers to carbon talks, tacitly obey the carbon and other pollutant budgets the watersheds, as dominant actors, lay down for them, and cheat when they think they can evade detection. Their relative lack of power means they must file impact reports for approval by neighboring regional watershed consortia in cases where projects might have an impact beyond the fencelines.

Most of the corporations’ former economic functions, aside from a dwindling number of areas in which they still possess a monopoly on the necessary technical expertise, have been taken over by the watersheds. Some pre-watershed industrial resources have been absorbed by the watersheds — e.g. “MIT and the Pan-Asian Maker Collective” are “hooked into the dandelion networks.”

Overall, relations between watersheds and corporations amount to a cold war.

“We still buy from them, sometimes….. Things we need that we haven’t been able to back-engineer yet, or exchanges that someone thinks will eventually incentivize them to join us. And they’re allowed out among the watersheds as long as they promise to behave.”

The watersheds’ primary focus in dealing with the corporations is managing their decline — taking over their remaining indispensable functions, and in the meantime maintaining contact to encourage internal culture change and preventing any desperate rear-guard action that will get a lot of people killed.

“They’re not going to disappear any time soon — someone has to keep talking to them, or they’ll never change enough to join the rest of the world….

“We still need them. They almost broke the world, when they had power — but the corporations still make key parts of our network infrastructure. They think they need us because without those exports, they lose any justification for their continued existence. But really, that tenuous connection is their last chance to find a new justification …

author: Alexandra Bradbury
title: Letter Carriers Set to Deliver Change in Upcoming Union Election
content:
A leadership change looks likely in the Letter Carriers (NALC) this fall. Members are mad about low pay and forced overtime, dangerous heat and robberies, the rejected contract imposed last year, the backlog of tens of thousands of grievances, and the president’s secretive approach to bargaining.

There’s not just one group pushing for change, but a whole ecosystem of reform groups, slates, and podcasters among the 5,000-plus delegates coming to Los Angeles for the union convention August 3-7. They’ll rub elbows and hopefully build unity at a “ Reformers Rum Party ” on Sunday night, the eve of the convention.

Days before the August 5 nominations, it looks like a three-way race for president. The 200,000 members will get the chance to vote this fall—by mail ballot, of course—for 10 officers, three trustees, and 15 regional business agents.

Two reform tickets have been campaigning for two years. One is the Concerned Letter Carriers (CLC) slate, headlined by current Vice President James Henry and including a number of branch (local) presidents. The other is Mike Caref , business agent for Illinois, running solo for president.

Despite months of speculation about whether President Brian Renfroe would run again, he still hasn’t made any announcment. But a third slate announced July 17 includes many other incumbents, led by Eddie Davidson, current business agent for Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas.

DOOMSDAY CLOCK

The backdrop is ongoing existential threats to USPS. Since Trump returned to office, the postal doomsday clock has been minutes from midnight .

Though Trump hasn’t acted on his threat to move the Postal Service under the Department of Commerce, his new batch of nominees for the Board of Governors aren’t even from private sector logistics, but from finance—so maybe less interested in rationalizing the service than in selling it for parts.

Postmaster General David Steiner, who somehow makes his predecessor Louis DeJoy look good, is going along with Trump’s extreme attacks on vote by mail. He says USPS won’t deliver ballots in states that won’t hand over voter lists to the government.

Steiner has also been claiming USPS could run out of money within the year, and threatening to close post offices and cut delivery days if its finances aren’t fixed.

The next-biggest union, the Postal Workers (APWU), organized rallies July 28 for three reforms that would help in the short term—raise the debt limit, modify the investment strategy for retiree benefit funds (they’re all in treasury bonds), and change how the retirement obligation is calculated.

Longer-term, USPS needs to adapt to fewer letters and more packages. Management’s approach has been to cut costs by degrading service. The unions argue it should instead expand revenue by adding services like banking, Internet access, hunting licenses, electric vehicle charging, and checking in on seniors.

In addition, retired letter carrier and longtime activist Jamie Partridge argues, the government should subsidize rural delivery, as many other countries do.

OVERLAPPING GROUPS

A vote-no movement on the 2024 contract was organized by a coalition of forces including Caref, the CLC, the Build a Fighting NALC (BFN) caucus, and influential podcaster Corey Walton, number two on the CLC ticket.

Podcasts are big with letter carriers—you can listen while you slog through the workday. One called “Next Generation Carriers” has interviewed activists from all the vying groups and even Renfroe himself ( Labor Notes staffers have also been guests). Co-host Margo O’Neill, a steward of Branch 352 in Des Moines, is also the treasurer for BFN. Her main goals at the convention, she said, are to grow the reach of the reform movement and to build unity across the various existing groups.

The Next Gen hosts have been agitating for a contract demand of “30 for 30”: a starting wage of $30 and no more than one manager per 30 carriers, to save money and alleviate micromanagement. New carriers start at about $21 , in an entry-level job called “city carrier assistant” where they’re often made to work Sundays delivering Amazon packages. It can take two years to convert to a career position, and even then, everyone hired since 2013 is on second-tier Table 2 pay.

author: Antimilitaristisches Aktionsnetzwerk (a2n)
title: Freispruch wegen Adbustings gegen Bundeswehr-Naziprepper
content:
Soldaten der Bundeswehr als „Nazi-Prepper“ zu bezeichnen? „Ist ok!“ entschied das Amtsgericht Schwerin. Denn die Meinungsfreiheit gelte auch für Adbustings, die die Bundeswehr kritisieren. Die Staatsanwaltschaft zieht nun ihre zuvor eingereichte Berufung zurück. Kai  N. Krieger vom Antimilitaristischen Aktionsnetzwerk (a2n) freut sich: „Zu Recht endet diese Farce eines  Prozesses mit einer Schlappe für die Staatsanwaltschaft. Dieser Kriminalisierungsversuch war skandalös. Ab jetzt sollte sich der Staatsapparat um die Nazi-Prepper kümmern, anstatt diejenigen zu verurteilen, die die Botschaft übermitteln.“

Beleidigung wegen Bundeswehr-Adbustings?

Das Amtsgericht Schwerin hat am Dienstag, den 10.03.2026 zwei Antimilitaristen freigesprochen. Daraufhin legte die Staatsanwaltschaft Berufung ein. Sie hatte den Aktivisten „Beleidigung aller aktiven Soldaten der Bundeswehr“ vorgeworfen. Jetzt hat die Staatsanwaltschaft die Berufung zurückgezogen. Der Freispruch ist damit rechtsgültig. Im Jahr zuvor kritisierten Antimilitarist*innen in Schwerin und in weiteren 15 deutschen Städten den zum ersten Mal stattfindenden Veteranentag. Dafür platzierten sie unerlaubt eigene Poster im Design der Bundeswehr in Werbevitrinen. Mit Sprüchen wie: „Abhängen mit Nazi-Preppern? Nein zum Veteranentag!“ und „Deutscher Mix: Nazis, Patronen, Einzelfälle“ machten sie auf das Nazi-Problem in der Bundeswehr aufmerksam.

https://antimil-aktionsnetzwerk.site36.net/2025/06/15/adbusting-protest-gegen-den-veteranentag-in-13-staedten/

Adbusting-Alarm im Naziprepper-Land

Schwerin: Das ist die Hauptstadt der Naziprepper vom Nordkreuz. Die Mitglieder der Terrorbande waren Polizisten, Militärs, Juristen und Politiker. Sie klauten Waffen und Munition bei ihren Arbeitgeber*innen, legten Todeslisten mit Namen und Adressen an, und bestellten bereits Löschkalk und Leichensäcke. Besonders brisant: Der Chef der Heimatschutzkompanie, die wenige Wochen später Liegenschaften beim G20-Gipfel in Hamburg unterstützen sollte, ist beteiligt. Er wollte den Nazi-Preppern für ihre geplanten Mordtaten Papiere und LKWs der Bundeswehr zur Verfügung stellen.

Ausgerechnet bei den Cops in Mecklenburg sorgte die Adbusting- Aktion für Großalarm. Begründung: „ Bundeswehrfeindliche Plakate“ Im Strafgesetzbuch gibt es keinen Paragrafen, der eine eventuelle „Bundeswehrfeindschaft“ verbietet . Die Polizeiinspektion Stralsund meint (https://www.presseportal.de/blaulicht/pm/108767/6054960) jedoch: „ (…)diese Art des kreativen Protestes ist keineswegs ein satirischer Witz, sondern kann vielmehr den Tatbestand von Ordnungswidrigkeiten oder auch Straftaten erfüllen.“ „Es wäre schön, wenn die Mecklenburger Cops ihre Nazi-Prepper-Kollegen, die Mitglied in der Nazi-Terror-Bande „Nordkreuz“ waren, so engagiert verfolgen und rausschmeißen würden.“  kommentiert dies Kai N. Krieger.

„Auch unbequemes Adbusting ist grundrechtlich geschützt“

Die Werbevitrinen im öffentlichen Raum lassen sich mit handelsüblichen Rohsteckschlüsseln aus dem Baumarkt öffnen. Daher scheiden Sachbeschädigung und Diebstahl bereits aus. Deswegen versuchte die Staatsanwaltschaft Schwerin, die Adbustings als „Beleidigung aller aktiven Soldaten“ zu übersehen. Was die Staatsanwaltschaft bei ihrer Verfolgung Unschuldiger übersah: Genau das ist erlaubt:  Das Bundesverfassungsgericht stellte u.a. im bekannten Urteil zu  „Soldaten sind Mörder!“ im Jahr 1995 klar, dass man so etwas sagen darf, ohne bestraft zu werden. Denn „alle Soldaten“ sei keine hinreichend zählbare Einschränkung, so dass sich eine konkrete Soldat*in beleidigt fühlen müsse. Auch Politik und Institutionen dürfen straffrei beleidigt werden.

„Auch unbequemes Adbusting ist grundrechtlich geschützt“ schreibt Prof. Dr. Fischer-Lescano in einem Gutachten dazu:

https://verfassungsblog.de/adbusting-unbequem-aber-grundrechtlich-geschuetzt/

Folgerichtig erklärte auch das Bundesverfassungsgericht aus Karlsruhe im Dezember 2023 eine Hausdurchsuchung der Berliner Polizei wegen Adbustings für illegal:

https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/DE/2023/bvg23-121.html
